articles.title: Humour, passion, connection: Montreal Comiccon celebrates summer edition
articles.text:
Humour, passion, connection: Montreal Comiccon celebrates summer edition
In this photo essay from Canada, we showcase the creativity of participants at this must-attend annual comics convention.
Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,010 posts, we featured an art festival, cartoon gallery. world music festival, telecom expo, millets fair, climate change expo, wildlife conference, startup festival, Diwali rangoli, and jazz festival.
This summer, Montreal Comiccon held its annual convention at Palais des Congrès in downtown Montreal. The multi-genre pop culture convention showcases the best in comic books, sci-fi, toys, movies, video games, and other entertainment IP, along with cosplay (costume and play) competitions.
An estimated 60,000 attendees flock to the three-day event, which includes an exhibition hall, artist alley, corporate booths, expert panels, and film screenings for pop culture fans of all ages. The event attracts the anglophone as well as francophone population markets of Montreal, thus serving as a bridge between US, Canadian and French markets.
Each year, an estimated 50 countries and 150 cities around the world host events centred around the culture and business of comics (see our earlier coverage of Comic Con India here). Montreal is also host to one of the world’s largest jazz festivals, the Montreal International Jazz Festival (see our coverage of earlier editions of the festival from 2015 onwards here).
Montreal Comiccon serves as a gathering place for people who share a passion for storytelling, creativity and imaginative worlds. It appeals to lifelong comic book readers as well as newcomers discovering the world of superheroes and fantasy.
As shown in this photo essay, people from different ages come together to celebrate the characters and stories they love. The welcoming atmosphere spills over into nearby parks, cafes and metro stations, and encourages friendships through self-expression.
The comics industry has played a significant role in shaping popular culture for well over a century. Comics combine visual art with storytelling, creating a unique medium that appeals to a diverse spectrum of readers. It effectively combines entertainment, education and inspiration.
One of the comics industry's greatest strengths is its ability to communicate complex ideas through words, images and animation. Readers can easily follow action and character development while enjoying vibrant artwork. Because of this accessibility, comics often encourage literacy among young readers.
The comics industry has also become a major economic force. Successful comic book characters have expanded into blockbuster films, television series, streaming shows, video games, toys, and merchandise. These adaptations generate billions of dollars worldwide while introducing comic stories to new audiences.
Independent creators have also benefited from the industry's growth. Modern publishing platforms allow artists and writers to share original stories without relying solely on major publishers.
Graphic novels now cover a wide range of genres, including history, memoir, science fiction, romance, horror, and educational topics. This demonstrates that comics are far more than superhero adventures.
One of the most exciting aspects of comic conventions is the practice of dressing up as fictional characters from comics, movies, television, anime, and video games. For many participants, cosplay is much more than wearing a costume – it is a creative hobby that combines craftsmanship, performance and personal expression.
Preparing customised costumes teaches valuable skills such as sewing, painting, sculpting, problem-solving, and attention to detail. Completing a costume provides a strong sense of accomplishment and pride.
Wearing a costume also allows participants to step into the role of a beloved character. Children and adults alike enjoy pretending to be superheroes, villains, fantasy warriors, or animated characters. This playful experience encourages imagination and confidence, allowing people to express themselves in ways they might not in everyday life.
Cosplay also creates a welcoming sense of community. Participants often compliment each other's work, exchange crafting tips, and pose together for photographs. Many friendships begin simply because two people recognise a shared favorite character or series.
Perhaps most importantly, costumes help create the magical atmosphere that makes Comic Con events around the world so memorable. Walking through the convention feels like stepping into a world where fictional universes come to life.
Every space is filled with colorful characters, smiling fans and creative designs. For participants, dressing up is not only fun but also a celebration of imagination, creativity, fandom, and the joy of sharing their passions with others.
Now what have you done today to pause in your busy schedule and harness your creative side for a better world?
(All photographs taken by Madanmohan Rao on location in Montreal.)

articles.title: Superchargeurs Tesla gratuits en Gironde, taxes sur les PHEV et un long trajet trop facile en citadine électrique : le récap’ Vroom de la semaine
articles.text:
Face aux incendies, Tesla rend 9 stations Superchargeurs gratuites en France et en Espagne
- Tesla a activé gratuitement et automatiquement neuf Superchargeurs proches des incendies (cinq en Gironde : Arès, Biganos, Mérignac, Bordeaux Lac, Bègles ; quatre en Espagne) du 29 juillet minuit au 5 août minuit pour faciliter l’évacuation.
- Ouverte à tous les automobilistes et indiquée à « 0 € » dans l’application, l’opération illustre la capacité unique de Tesla à modifier en quelques clics la tarification de son réseau grâce à son contrôle de bout en bout.
- Répété lors de catastrophes antérieures (Japon, Ukraine, inondations, ouragans), ce geste conjugue assistance humanitaire et avantage réputationnel face à des réseaux concurrents qui n’imitent pas ce réflexe.
« Nous n’avons pas de temps à perdre », le patron de Volkswagen appelle l’UE à taxer les hybrides rechargeables chinois
- Les hybrides rechargeables chinois ont atteint 27,3 % des immatriculations PHEV en Europe au premier semestre 2026.
- Oliver Blume demande que l’Union européenne impose dans les mois à venir des droits de douane sur les PHEV chinois équivalents à ceux appliqués aux voitures électriques.
- Actuellement les PHEV chinois restent soumis au tarif douanier standard de 10 %, contre jusqu’à 35 % pour les BEV, créant une faille réglementaire exploitée par les constructeurs chinois.
Longs trajets en Nissan Micra ou R5 : c’est presque trop simple
- Avec la batterie 52 kWh, la Micra a couvert les 480 km Mulhouse–Paris en n’exigeant que deux arrêts recharge d’une quarantaine de minutes au total.
- Le planificateur Google/Renault s’est montré d’une fiabilité redoutable, les estimations d’état de charge collant à moins de 2 % de la réalité et supprimant la charge mentale du trajet.
- La citadine a atteint un pic de charge DC de 100 kW — même en se branchant à 36 % —, ce qui explique des temps d’arrêt étonnamment courts pour ce segment.

articles.title: Votre Garmin ou votre Apple Watch vous irrite le poignet ? Trois réflexes suffisent
articles.text:
Sur TikTok, des marathoniens exhibent fièrement la marque laissée par leur montre après l’effort, jusqu’à ce que les commentaires les alertent sur un mot peu ragoûtant : le « watch rot ». Derrière la tendance virale se cache une réalité dermatologique banale, largement évitable pour peu qu’on adopte les bons réflexes.
Il y a quelque chose d’ironique à porter un bracelet bardé de capteurs censés veiller sur sa santé, et à négliger le seul organe qui, lui, encaisse le contact permanent : la peau du poignet. C’est pourtant le paradoxe qu’une vague de vidéos a mis en lumière au début de l’été 2026. Des coureurs filment le dessous de leur montre Garmin après une longue sortie, dévoilant une peau rougie, parfois luisante, que les internautes ont baptisée « watch rot », littéralement la peau qui pourrit sous la montre. Le terme est excessif, la panique aussi, mais le phénomène est réel et documenté depuis des années par les dermatologues. Voici ce qui se joue réellement sous le boîtier, et surtout comment l’éviter sans renoncer à son suivi d’activité.
Le watch rot décrypté, une dermatite de contact des plus banales
« Watch rot ». Un nouveau terme anglais parfait pour capter l’attention sur les réseaux sociaux alors que la réalité est plus prosaïque. Le « watch rot » n’est rien d’autre qu’une dermatite de contact, une irritation cutanée qui survient quand la peau réagit à un contact prolongé. Les dermatologues distinguent deux mécanismes. Le premier, de loin le plus fréquent, est la dermatite d’irritation : la sueur, les cellules mortes, les résidus de savon et la saleté se logent entre la peau et le bracelet, tandis que le frottement d’une sangle trop serrée fragilise la barrière cutanée. Le second, plus rare, est la dermatite allergique, une vraie réaction immunitaire à un matériau précis. Un cas clinique documenté décrivait ainsi une femme de 28 ans développant un eczéma récurrent au poignet, dont les tests ont confirmé qu’il provenait d'une boucle recouverte de nickel : les symptômes ont disparu après le passage à un bracelet en silicone sans partie métallique.
Le résultat, lui, se reconnaît vite : rougeurs, démangeaisons, peau qui pèle, petits boutons et parfois une sensation d’échauffement. Rien qui relève de la nécrose, malgré ce que le vocabulaire TikTok laisse entendre. Et surtout, rien qui soit propre à une marque en particulier. Si les vidéos virales pointaient massivement les montres connectées de Garmin, c’est d’abord un effet de communauté, celle des coureurs et triathlètes très équipés, pas une faiblesse technique du produit. Le phénomène touche potentiellement toutes les montres connectées, quel que soit le logo. La preuve, Apple reconnaît elle-même, dans sa documentation officielle, que ses boîtiers et bracelets contiennent des traces de nickel et de méthacrylates, tout en assurant que les quantités restent sous les seuils problématiques pour la majorité des utilisateurs. L’auteur de ces lignes est lui-même touché. Depuis le début de cet été, en portant une Apple Watch ou une Galaxy Watch. Rien à voir donc avec la marque de votre équipement.
Pour agir efficacement, encore faut-il cerner les vrais responsables, et ils sont presque toujours les mêmes. La sueur arrive en tête. Piégée sous un bracelet non respirant, elle macère au contact de la peau et crée un terrain idéal pour l’irritation, d’autant que l’humidité ne peut pas s’évaporer. C’est la raison pour laquelle le problème explose après l’effort ou pendant le sommeil, ces longues plages où la montre ne quitte jamais le poignet. Le serrage constitue le deuxième facteur, et le plus contre-intuitif : pour capter un rythme cardiaque fiable, le capteur optique doit être plaqué contre la peau, ce qui pousse beaucoup d’utilisateurs à trop serrer. Or une sangle trop tendue multiplie les frottements et coupe la circulation de l’air. Un indice ne trompe pas : si le boîtier laisse une empreinte marquée sur la peau une fois retiré, c'est qu’il était trop serré.
Le troisième coupable découle des deux premiers, l’absence de respiration, quand une montre portée vingt-quatre heures sur vingt-quatre ne laisse jamais au poignet le temps de récupérer. S’y ajoutent des facteurs souvent ignorés, comme les crèmes solaires, lotions et parfums appliqués sous le bracelet, dont certains composants réagissent avec les matériaux de la sangle ou en attaquent le revêtement protecteur.
Nettoyer, desserrer, faire respirer, le trio qui sauve la peau
La première solution est aussi la moins glamour : laver sa montre, et son poignet, régulièrement. Un bracelet en silicone se rince à l’eau claire et se sèche complètement avant d’être remis, et en cas de résidus incrustés, un peu d’alcool à friction sur un chiffon fait l’affaire avant rinçage. Le boîtier se nettoie de la même façon, avec un chiffon non pelucheux. Point important, on évite sur le silicone les produits agressifs comme le gel hydroalcoolique ou le savon pour les mains, qui abîment le matériau à la longue. Pour les bracelets en cuir, la règle change : on les tient éloignés de l'eau et on se contente d’un chiffon légèrement humide, séché à l’air libre.
Pour soulager la peau, un nettoyage doux suffit, avec un lave-mains hypoallergénique pour éviter les résidus de tensioactifs, suivi d’une lotion hydratante légère. Ce geste, qui prend quelques secondes, est pourtant celui que la plupart des utilisateurs zappent le plus volontiers, comme le soulignaient sans ménagement certains commentaires sous les vidéos virales, rappelant qu’il est paradoxal d’acheter un objet dédié à la santé pour négliger celle de la peau qui se trouve juste dessous. Petit conseil d’ami : si votre peau est déjà bien abîmée, un peu de crème cicatrisante durant deux à trois jours permet de récupérer un épiderme parfaitement hydraté.
La deuxième parade tient dans la façon de porter la montre. La bonne tension est celle qui maintient le capteur au contact du poignet sans l’étrangler : ni assez lâche pour que le boîtier glisse, ni assez serré pour marquer la peau. Un test simple consiste à vérifier qu’un doigt peut se glisser entre le bracelet et le poignet. Autre réflexe précieux, desserrer légèrement la sangle pendant les phases de repos, notamment la nuit, ce qui n’altère pas la précision du suivi de sommeil à condition de ne pas tomber dans l’excès inverse et de la laisser pendouiller. Tout est affaire de dosage.
Faire respirer la peau constitue le troisième levier : retirer la montre pendant les périodes d’inactivité, ne serait-ce que vingt minutes par jour, offre un répit salutaire, et alterner de poignet une semaine sur deux répartit la contrainte, à condition de penser à indiquer le changement dans l’application pour préserver la fiabilité des mesures. Quand l’irritation s’installe malgré tout, la seule vraie solution consiste à cesser de porter la montre le temps que la peau cicatrise, quelques jours parfois, quelques semaines dans les cas les plus tenaces. Le retirer avant la douche relève aussi du bon sens : la montre reste au sec, et l’on sèche le poignet avant de la remettre. Vous n’avez pas besoin de lire vos notifications sous la douche, prenez un instant pour vous.
Changer de bracelet ou consulter, les recours quand rien ne suffit
Quand l’hygiène et le réglage ne suffisent pas, le matériau du bracelet devient suspect. Le silicone d’origine, comme les bracelets tiers du même type, concentre souvent les réactions, à la fois parce qu’il ne respire pas et parce que certaines peaux y sont sensibles. Le passage à un bracelet en nylon tissé, plus respirant, améliore nettement la situation pour beaucoup d’utilisateurs, même si les épisodes peuvent encore survenir ponctuellement. Les modèles en tissu offrent une alternative comparable.
Pour les peaux les plus sensibles, une couche fine de crème barrière hypoallergénique appliquée avant le port peut limiter le contact direct avec la sangle, sans toutefois dispenser des autres précautions. Et si le doute d’une allergie persiste, notamment au nickel, un test épicutané chez un dermatologue permet d’identifier l’allergène précis et d’orienter les choix futurs.
Car au fond, la question n’est pas de savoir s’il faut renoncer à sa montre connectée, mais de reconnaître qu’un objet porté en permanence mérite le même entretien que celui qu’on accorde à ses chaussures de sport ou à ses écouteurs. La technologie surveille le corps, encore faut-il accepter de surveiller un peu la technologie en retour.

articles.title: Kioxia CM10 Series Launched for the PCIe Gen6 Generation of SSDs
articles.text:
Ahead of FMS 2026, Kioxia launched its new CM10 series, marking the company’s entry into PCIe 6.0 enterprise storage with direct liquid cooling capability for AI infrastructure deployments. These new SSDs leverage Kioxia’s BiCS FLASH generation 10 memory technology and target high-performance KV cache workloads alongside NVIDIA CMX context memory solutions.
Kioxia CM10 Series Specifications and Features
This new CM10 series delivers substantial performance gains over the previous CM9 generation, with Kioxia claiming up to approximately 92 percent higher sequential read performance and up to approximately 85 percent higher random read performance. These improvements address the scaling demands of AI models approaching trillions of parameters and context windows expanding to millions of tokens.
KIOXIA offers the CM10 series across multiple form factors to accommodate different deployment requirements. Its E3.S and E1.S variants support direct-cold-plate liquid cooling for specific thickness profiles, while all forms remain compatible with traditional air-cooled environments. The EDSFF lineup includes E3.S at 7.5 mm thickness and E1.S in both 9.5 mm and 15 mm profiles. 9.5 mm variants of both form factors support direct liquid cooling environments. There is also a dual-port design in E3.S for high availability for traditional HA storage arrays.
A 2.5″ option extends the CM10 Series to conventional enterprise chassis that cannot accommodate EDSFF forms or require higher capacity per drive slot. The 2.5″ CM6 is 15mm in thickness and maintains a dual-port design like the E3.S variant for high availability applications. Something interesting from the slides is that the 2.5″ is listed as using BiCS FLASH generation 8 TLC flash memory with PCIe 5.0 compliance, rather than the Gen 10 memory and PCIe 6.0 interface found in EDSFF models. On STH, we have been warning that the traditional U.2/ U.3 drives were likely to start giving way to EDSFF connectors as the electrical requirements of PCIe Gen6 hit. This is a great example of that.
Final Words
We expect to see the Kioxia CM10 series drives in AI storage tier deployments where ephemeral KV cache benefits from flash latency between GPU HBM and networked storage. Still, the new announcement is important since we are seeing chips like the NVIDIA Vera CPU and the AMD EPYC Venice series hit the market. The new CM10 series represents Kioxia’s response to AI infrastructure storage demands that extend beyond traditional enterprise SSD requirements. Direct liquid-cooling capability addresses thermal constraints in dense GPU pods, where KV cache storage sits adjacent to accelerator racks. Its performance claims against the CM9 generation suggest meaningful headroom for context memory workloads that NVIDIA CMX solutions target.
Perhaps most notable is that we are finally seeing a split in NVMe SSDs away from around a decade and a half of 2.5″ U.2 form factors leading the way. Separating PCIe 6.0 EDSFF forms from PCIe 5.0 2.5″ variants allows Kioxia to serve both next-generation liquid-cooled deployments and existing air-cooled infrastructure with a single product family branding. The use of BiCS FLASH generation 10 in EDSFF form factors versus generation 8 in 2.5″ form factors reflects the thermal and density requirements. Perhaps we will see more of that with PCIe Gen5 drives using older NAND generations, while Gen6 drives use newer ones.

articles.title: Alors que les prix des PC s'envolent, ce laptop Lenovo (OLED + Ultra 7) s'offre une remise de 170 €
articles.text:
Trouver un ordinateur portable bien équipé sans exploser son budget devient un vrai casse-tête. Entre la crise de la RAM et la flambée des prix des composants qui s’intensifie, les bons rapports qualité-prix se font plus rares. Le Lenovo Yoga Slim 7 14ILL10 tire pourtant son épingle du jeu avec une dalle OLED et un processeur Intel Core Ultra 7, le tout dans un châssis fin et léger. Et côté prix, il profite d’une réduction de près de 170 euros sur Amazon.
Les points forts du Lenovo Yoga Slim 7 14ILL10
- Son châssis fin et léger et son écran OLED
- Un processeur Intel Core Ultra 7 polyvalent
- Une autonomie solide
Habituellement proposé à 1 099,99 euros, le Lenovo Yoga Slim 7 14ILL10 s’affiche actuellement en promotion à 930,99 euros sur Amazon.
Vous vouliez un ordinateur portable d’exception ? Les PC équipés de Snapdragon tiennent leurs promesses.
Un écran OLED de 14 pouces dans un format compact
L’un des atouts les plus intéressants de cet ultrabook Lenovo est son écran OLED de 14 pouces avec une définition de 1 920 x 1 200 pixels. Il offre des couleurs vives et brillantes, tout en proposant des noirs profonds, assurant un très bon contraste et une bonne gestion de la copywriting. Pour du montage photo, de la retouche ou simplement du confort visuel au quotidien, c’est un vrai plus par rapport à un écran IPS classique.
Il plaît aussi pour ses finitions et son format compact. Avec une épaisseur de 13,9 mm et un poids de seulement 1,19 kg, c’est un laptop qui se glisse facilement dans un sac pour les trajets quotidiens entre le domicile et le travail. Malgré sa finesse, le Yoga Slim 7 14ILL10 est bien équipé en termes de connectique : il propose deux ports Thunderbolt 4, un port HDMI 2.1, un port USB-A, un lecteur de carte SD et une prise casque (3,5 mm).
Un Intel Core Ultra 7 qui assure au quotidien
Le design et la qualité d’image sont au rendez-vous, de même que les performances. Sous le capot, on a le processeur Intel Core Ultra 7 256V épaulé par 16 Go de mémoire vive. Ce n’est pas une machine pensée pour le jeu vidéo exigeant, mais pour un usage polyvalent et productif, la puissance est largement suffisante.
N’oublions pas d’ailleurs le SSD de 1 To qui se charge quant à lui d’assurer des temps de chargement réduits et des lancements rapides de la machine pour gagner en réactivité.
Le constructeur a également fait de beaux efforts sur l’autonomie. Pour son petit gabarit, il accueille une batterie de 70 Wh qui offre jusqu’à 34 heures d’autonomie, de quoi l’utiliser sans avoir à le recharger fréquemment. Et si vous êtes en rade de batterie, n’ayez crainte, le Yoga Slim 7 est compatible avec la charge rapide : il est possible de récupérer trois heures d’autonomie avec seulement 15 minutes de recharge.
Si vous souhaitez comparer ce modèle à d’autres références du marché, nous vous invitons à consulter notre guide des meilleurs PC ultraportables du moment.

articles.title: Balance Theory Raises $19 Million to Help Enterprises Manage Cybersecurity Investments
articles.text:
Cybersecurity investment management startup Balance Theory has raised $19 million in Series A funding to expand its platform for helping CISOs evaluate and manage security spending.
Balance Theory’s platform is designed to bring cybersecurity investment planning, market intelligence and execution into a single system. It maintains contextual information about an organization’s security program, supplements it with proprietary market data, and employs AI agents and automated workflows to support purchasing and portfolio-management decisions.
As the company explains, “Balance theory manages security investment events end-to-end. Detect investment decision triggers, run each event for the best cost and coverage outcome, and continuously rationalize the program to maximize the impact of every dollar deployed.”
The platform also creates a record explaining why individual investments were made and monitors for changes that could affect their value, suitability or priority. According to the company, its technology currently manages more than $1 billion in cybersecurity spending.
The funding round was led by SYN Ventures, with participation from existing investors DataTribe and TEDCO. The company also announced that Dan Burns, founder of Accuvant and former CEO of Optiv, has joined as executive chairman.
Balance Theory said it will use the new funding to accelerate go-to-market efforts, build deeper enterprise integrations, expand its cybersecurity market intelligence, and continue developing the platform’s AI agents and skills.
The Columbia, Maryland-based company raised $3 million in Seed funding back in 2022.
“Security leaders lacked a consistent way to understand their own enterprise, navigate an increasingly complex market and connect those insights to action,” Balance Theory co-founder and CEO Greg Baker said.
The company did not disclose its valuation following the investment.

articles.title: Temporal 5x’d AI spend and doubled revenue. CEO Samar Abbas says he can’t prove they’re connected.
articles.text:
Temporal 5x’d AI spend and doubled revenue. CEO Samar Abbas says he can’t prove they’re connected.
Temporal co-founder and CEO Samar Abbas is guiding the company’s adoption of AI tools across engineering and business workflows. (Credit: The New Stack photo illustration)
For the final two weeks of the year, Temporal clears its calendars. The company calls it a reading period: no meetings, just time to explore, learn, and build. Over the ‘25 holidays, co-founder and CTO Maxim Fateev spent his time with coding agents. He came back describing work that once took six months, now done in less than thirty days, according to the company. Co-founder and CEO Samar Abbas credits that break with setting the company’s AI posture for the year. A fellow co-founder returning with numbers like that, he says, is a stronger argument than any company directive.
That shift, from a veteran engineer to a veteran engineer with Claude Code, led Abbas toward redirecting the company’s efforts. Temporal sells durable execution, the failure-resistant plumbing that keeps long-running software alive through crashes and outages, and it sells it to companies that cannot afford downtime. Nvidia and Netflix are among the companies using its workflow technology.
In February, the company raised $300 million at a $5 billion valuation on the promise that it can make agentic AI reliable for everyone else. Abbas, Temporal’s CEO who swapped roles with now-CTO Fateev in 2024, decided the company had to prove that on its own first. He calls the effort “AI for Temporal.”
AI adoption as a job requirement
“We are a company of builders, which means it’s not just engineering,” Abbas tells The New Stack. “The entire company needs to re-evaluate how business gets done and how it uses these tools.”
At more than 500 people — 200 of them engineers — that is a lot of re-evaluating. The burden lands on every employee, he says: Examine your own daily workflow, bring some curiosity to the tools, and change how the job gets done. The expectation is not optional, and Abbas was blunt about it to me. Temporal does not mandate a single product, but it does expect people to change how they work.
“If you are still not adopting the right tools to get better, you don’t have a role here at Temporal.”
“If you are still not adopting the right tools to get better, you don’t have a role here at Temporal,” he says. The requirement isn’t to use a specific product, but rather a mandate to adopt the work.
He frames that around growth rather than headcount. Temporal is spending to unlock new work, Abbas says, not to run the same company with fewer people. He does not rank employees on a usage leaderboard because he thinks it creates the wrong incentive. The demand also cuts against the company’s own grain.
Abbas asking Temporal employees to turn experimental without turning reckless, and he says that cultural shift is the harder half of the work.
One of Temporal’s core values is what Abbas calls “reliable as gravity.” Temporal is conservative when it bets on a technical stack. He is asking it to turn experimental without turning reckless, and he says that cultural shift is the harder half of the work.
Temporal
Samar Abbas · Co-founder & CEO
- Claude Code: the default coding tool, adopted on its own after the holidays
- Cursor plus foundation models mostly from OpenAI and Anthropic
- Open-weight models not approved internally; deemed unproven on security and privacy
- Claude Desktop puts app-building in non-technical hands
- Notion + MCP as the shared knowledge base; Slack AI for status
- Built in-house on Temporal: Deputy (security workflow) and model routers
- Vendor costs tracked in Vantage, with hard spending limits
- Finance and engineering review the outliers every two weeks
- No employee token leaderboards, by design
- No absolute dollar figure on the record
- 500+ employees, 200+ engineers, fully remote
- Every function must rebuild its own workflows, not just engineering
- No mandated tool and no usage leaderboard
- Blunt line: adapt or “you don’t have a role here at Temporal”
- Framed as growth, not headcount cuts
- BDR is the most AI-native team; outbound runs as Temporal workloads, hours to minutes
- Revenue roughly doubled this year, by Abbas’s account
- No direct correlation established between AI use and the revenue
- Recruiting prep also compressed from hours to minutes
- Cheap generation collapsed the cost of producing sloppy work
- Reviewers, not authors, became the bottleneck
- Unreviewed AI work reached slide decks and even websites
- Fix is cultural: self-review before you hand off
“It’s not about shipping features faster. It’s about shipping value customers care about.”
Samar Abbas, Co-founder & CEO
On why faster shipping is not the same as value, a gap he says he still cannot measure.
On the engineering side, the tooling is deliberately unmandated. Temporal enables the tier-one options, Cursor and foundation models mostly from OpenAI and Anthropic, and lets engineers settle on what works. Claude Code became the dominant choice on its own after the ‘25 holidays, Abbas says.
What the company has not done is bring open weights inside. Temporal has not broadly approved open-weight models for internal use, which Abbas says remain unproven for its security and privacy requirements. There is no formal model-review process yet; a central AI team vets each new model for security before it is opened up across the company.
Tools beyond engineering
Abbas splits the company into two adoption problems: the technical users and everyone else, and puts the same demand on both. The most surprising adoption is happening away from the engineers. Abbas tells me a nontechnical member of Temporal’s recruiting team used Claude Desktop to build recruiting tools of their own, a job-description builder and an interview-plan builder that turned hours of scattered prep into a running start.
That project is growing into a sourcing agent that pulls and pushes candidate data across Notion and spreadsheets and ranks matches. The knowledge the sourcing agent draws on lives in Notion, wired through MCP into the company’s other systems of record. For a 500-person remote company, that wiring has done more for the non-technical side than any coding tool, letting low-code users reach systems they could not touch before, with whole workflows migrating into Notion pages as a result.
Day-to-day coordination runs through Slack, where Abbas says its AI features have replaced much of his old habit of pinging people for a status update.
Abbas smiles when he tells me the clearest payoff so far is not in engineering at all. Temporal’s business-dev reps, the team that researches prospects and drafts outbound messages, have become the most AI-native group in the company. Work that used to take hours, pulling data from a dozen places and turning it into a first outreach draft, now runs as a custom workload the team builds on Temporal and finishes in minutes. It is the AI-for-Temporal idea: a non-engineering team building on the company’s own infrastructure to turn a slow, manual process into a fast one. What excites Abbas is the loop as much as the saved hours.
Review bottlenecks and AI slop
Like at other organizations, Temporal is seeing AI improve processes but also shift bottlenecks. Point AI at one workload, clear the obvious constraint, and the bottleneck jumps somewhere else. Write more code and review becomes the choke point. It’s the pattern Abbas has become an expert at, and it’s why he distrusts easy wins.
The place it bit was where a reliability company like Temporal would least tolerate it. When code got cheap to produce, reviews got expensive. “AI slop is a real thing,” Abbas says. AI, he argued, has lowered the cost of producing sloppy work so much that reviewers are being flooded with it.
On critical infrastructure, the bar has not moved: Every line still gets read by a person before it’s committed, which makes the reviewer, not the author, the new constraint. It is a squeeze other engineering leaders are feeling, too. Temporal’s fix is cultural. It has made it acceptable to send work back the moment it’s clear the author did not read it themselves first. The slop is not only in code. Abbas has seen unreviewed AI-generated competitor analysis land in slide decks, and similarly sloppy material reach websites.
The AI bill is moving fast, too. AI costs have increased roughly fivefold this year, Abbas says, and most of the increase comes from coding agents. Temporal pulls every vendor charge into Vantage, sets hard ceilings, and every two weeks, finance and engineering meet over the outliers to decide, case by case, whose limits should rise or fall based on the usage patterns. What it will not do is turn that data into a scoreboard.
“A lot of companies created a dashboard of token consumption. We’re not big fans of that, because it creates this race where I need to become the leader in token consumption.”
“A lot of companies created a dashboard of token consumption,” Abbas says. “We’re not big fans of that, because it creates this race where I need to become the leader in token consumption.” Temporal keeps the usage data, he says, but does not expose it as an employee leaderboard or tie it to performance reviews.
Abbas recalled a runaway workflow at an earlier company that ran up $4 million in compute spending on AWS. Temporal’s answer is a value it calls “fly together”: Give people a budget, expect them to spend it like their own money, and catch the runaways with limits instead of shame.
Where the company did automate, it built the automation like software. Temporal’s security team used to file vulnerabilities as tickets and wait for engineers to prioritize them over feature work, which created constant friction between the teams. Now the team runs the whole lifecycle as one long-running durable workflow built on Temporal itself, an internal tool it calls Deputy: Find the flaw, generate the fix, open the PR, merge it, run CI, and roll it out. The security team’s role moved from filing issues to helping ship fixes.
Durable execution for agents
That internal work is also the commercial argument. The problem Temporal spent years on, keeping long-running work alive across failures, is the one many teams building production agents are now encountering.
“These agents are becoming more long-lived, more asynchronous, more mission-critical,” Abbas says. “That is exactly the problem space we’ve been trying to solve with durable execution.”
He describes Temporal’s core as an open foundation model: model-, language-, and cloud-agnostic, with an open-source server companies can run themselves. Inside Temporal, that has taken a solid form. Abbas says the company built an internal platform on Temporal where a non-technical employee can describe an app to Claude Desktop and deploy it in one click.
The guardrails, identity, security, and the MCP connections are wired in, and Temporal’s own model routers keep any single provider from becoming a dependency. The company used its Replay conference in May to make the same case to customers, where it introduced serverless workers, durable streaming, and other features positioned for agent workloads.
For all the speed, Abbas is unusually willing to say he cannot prove it is worth it. Engineering is shipping features 20% to 30% faster with the same-sized team, he says, and he says revenue has roughly doubled since the start of the year, though he is careful to add that he has established no direct correlation between the two.
“It’s not about shipping features faster. It’s about shipping value customers care about.”
He is skeptical of the tidy productivity numbers, that counts of PRs and lines of code, that are supposed to justify the bill. And he thinks the old founder playbook is part of what broke. The advice he got from investors was to do first-principles thinking on product and hire good leaders to run finance, hiring, and go-to-market the standard way. In the AI era, he says, that is backward. The functions everyone used to copy from a playbook are the ones now worth reworking from the start.
Which leaves the number he wants and does not have. “It’s not about shipping features faster. It’s about shipping value customers care about,” Abbas says. And he has yet to see a metric that directly connects the company’s AI use to that outcome.
Temporal knows what the tools cost. It knows they make the company faster. What it still cannot prove is that its customers can absorb the output. For now, that is the bottleneck no agent has cleared.

articles.title: New York is suing prediction market Kalshi, calling it an illegal gambling operation
articles.text:
Cutting corners: New York Attorney General Letitia James has sued prediction market platform Kalshi, alleging that it violates state gambling laws. The lawsuit, filed in the New York Supreme Court in Manhattan, claims the company runs an "illegal, unlicensed gambling operation" covering sports, culture, elections, and other events.
In a statement, James said Kalshi violates New York's anti-gambling laws, which are designed to protect minors from betting and combat gambling addiction in adults. "No matter what they call themselves, prediction markets like Kalshi are gambling platforms, plain and simple," she said, adding that Kalshi's actions are harming the most vulnerable New Yorkers.
The lawsuit asks the court to order Kalshi to forfeit all profits and pay restitution to New Yorkers who lost money on the platform. It also seeks fines equal to three times the company's gains. In total, the fines and damages New York is seeking amount to around $36 billion.
The lawsuit alleges that Kalshi is operating without a valid license from New York's Gaming Commission and has not paid state taxes, unlike licensed casinos and mobile sports gambling platforms. It also notes that Kalshi allows users as young as 18 to place wagers, while New York law requires bettors to be 21 or older to participate in mobile sports betting.
Talking to reporters, state officials argued that Kalshi's operations meet the textbook legal definition of gambling because "the outcomes of the events on which its users are betting are uncertain and outside the control of the bettor or hinge on a game of chance."
Kalshi has predictably rejected the allegations, calling the lawsuit little more than "political theater." In a statement, company spokesperson Elisabeth Diana argued that Kalshi's operations are regulated by federal law, and that states don't have the power to shut down a federally licensed exchange.
Diana also warned that shutting down Kalshi, which employs an estimated 125 to 150 people at its New York City headquarters, would end up hurting New Yorkers, since users would be pushed toward unregulated, offshore platforms instead. "We love New York, we love New Yorkers, and New Yorkers love our product," she added.
But New York is not the first state to sue Kalshi over illegal gambling and racketeering allegations.
At least 13 states, including Kentucky, Tennessee, Ohio, Wisconsin, Nevada, and Washington, have taken Kalshi and rival platforms like Polymarket to court over illegal gambling, tax evasion, underage betting, unfair competition, and other charges.
Masthead credit: ESPN

articles.title: Lost one-of-a-kind Nintendo DS cartridge hits eBay for $9,100 — PokePark Fishing Contest designed to delete itself after 12 hours, game so rare it was only distributed to theme park attendees in 2005
articles.text:
Lost one-of-a-kind Nintendo DS cartridge hits eBay for $9,100 — PokePark Fishing Contest designed to delete itself after 12 hours, game so rare it was only distributed to theme park attendees in 2005
PokePark Fishing Contest DS was a temporary, event‑exclusive Nintendo DS Download Play game that made the rounds in 2005.
A Nintendo DS game that was classified as ‘lost media’ for nearly two decades is currently within tantalizing reach of video gaming fans and archivists. All the fans need is about $9,100, and no rival bidders on an eBay auction for an ultra-rare, perhaps one-of-a-kind, development cartridge thought to contain the PokePark Fishing Contest DS minigame.
Japanese game archaeology enthusiast Yoshino @ Federation (renpou.com) shared details of the eBay auction and its significance to their tens of thousands of social media followers.
So, what’s the deal with PokePark Fishing Contest DS, and why is it ultra-rare or even classified as ‘lost media?’ This fishing mini-game was lost for several reasons. Firstly, it was a download-only title. Secondly, its distribution was limited to those attending a short-lived Pokémon theme park venue in Japan (PokePark 2005). It also eluded archivists because it would be removed from a DS handheld when it was powered off, or after a 12-hour limit, whichever triggered first.
The eBay listing shows a large development and testing cartridge, front and back. There’s also an image showing the cartridge working. However, the on-DS-screen proof of viability is limited to “a Japanese-language screen indicating a high-score ranking communication program.”
The Germany-located seller, catbearpaws, says the cart was acquired as part of a private lot, and is selling the hardware as-is, with no promises regarding functionality, compatibility, or provenance. Catbearpaws has a 100% selling record and is asking for bids starting at €7,999 ($9,100), with less than three days left to run. They also may accept offers via the eBay Make Offer button/process.
Our machine-translated version of the eBay listing screen content appears to confirm that this is indeed a dev cart that was used for hosting “PokePark Fishing Contest DS” assets of some kind. Whether a playable version of the game can be downloaded, transmitted, or extracted from this hardware remains to be seen. As mentioned, the seller isn’t guaranteeing anything about this expensive but potentially important retro gaming artifact.

articles.title: Todo lo que debes recordar del Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel para disfrutar mejor ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’
articles.text:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day, la nueva entrega de la saga del vecino amistoso de Nueva York, no solo es una gran película del querido héroe. También, es una de las mejores cintas de superhéroes de los últimos años. Y el motivo es evidente. La cinta, dirigida por Destin Daniel Cretton y con un guion escrito por Chris McKenna y Erik Sommers, es mucho más madura que sus antecesoras. También, la aventura callejera que los fanáticos del personaje esperaron por años. Una combinación que le brinda una especial personalidad a la producción.
Además, es la más cercana a la versión en viñeta del personaje, como bien destaca nuestra crítica. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day es, de hecho, la película que más sabe a cómic de toda la saga Holland. El cineasta asume al fin que Nueva York es un ingrediente indispensable para entender al héroe y plantea la ciudad como un nuevo microcosmos, mucho más cercano a los espectadores y a los lectores de viñetas. Es una ciudad viva, sobrestimulada, en la que el trepamuros se balancea por sus calles y edificios como pez en el agua.” Un elemento primordial para entender la nueva energía y vigor de la historia.
Con respecto al argumento, Spider-Man: Brand New Day explora con mayor libertad a sus protagonistas. Peter Parker se transforma gracias a Tom Holland en un héroe dividido por el deber y el dolor. Mientras que MJ (Zendaya) logra convertirse en el motivo por el cual el héroe debe buscar su redención. Algo que también incluye su amistad con Ned (Jacob Batalon), mucho más profunda y compleja. Junto al trío, la cinta incorpora a personajes icónicos como Frank Castle/Punisher (Jon Bernthal), el reverso oscuro de la moral de Peter. A la vez a Bruce Banner/Hulk (Mark Ruffalo) como conexión al Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel.
Mucho que contar en la nueva aventura de Spider-Man
Pero, claro está, Spider-Man: Brand New Day es parte del siempre creciente Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel. Y aunque la cinta está mucho más interesada en el personaje que en el multiverso (de ahí su éxito), todavía es parte de la saga. Tanto como para que su perspectiva sobre la mitología interconectada sea parte esencial y compleja sobre su historia. Eso, sin llegar a entorpecer la aventura mundana y muy cercana al héroe que cuenta.
No obstante, para entender mejor el argumento, te dejamos tres puntos que debes tener claros al momento de disfrutar de la película. Del motivo por el que Spider-Man es un extraño incluso para los más cercanos a sus nuevos aliados. Todo para que puedas disfrutar de Spider-Man: Brand New Day en toda su interesante premisa acerca del crecimiento, el poder y la responsabilidad con el futuro.
El hechizo de Doctor Strange y el olvido colectivo
Para comprender el punto de partida exacto de Spider-Man: Brand New Day, es fundamental recordar lo ocurrido en Spider-Man: No Way Home. Tras desatar un caos multiversal absoluto por alterar un conjuro místico, Peter Parker tomó una dolorosa y drástica decisión. La de pedir al Hechicero Supremo, Doctor Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch), que realizara un hechizo definitivo de olvido. Esta poderosa intervención mística borró por completo el recuerdo de su existencia real de la mente de absolutamente todas las personas del universo. Y peor aún, sin dejar ninguna excepción.
Debido a esto, sus seres más queridos, como MJ y su mejor amigo Ned Leeds, no tienen la menor idea acerca de su identidad. Tampoco que antes compartieron no solo amistad, sino también, docenas de aventuras heroicas. Un dato curioso: Peter intentó acercarse valientemente a ellos para revelarles la verdad oculta. Sin embargo, al verlos completamente felices, sonrientes y a salvo con sus nuevas vidas universitarias en el prestigioso MIT, prefirió mantenerse al margen. Además, sufrir el aislamiento absoluto para protegerlos de los peligros mortales que siempre lo persiguen.
Esta drástica realidad redefine por completo el propósito heroico de Peter. El peso de este anonimato total transforma su vida en una lucha psicológica constante por mantener su cordura. A la vez, su identidad como celoso protector de los inocentes neoyorquinos. De modo que el joven héroe debe aprender urgentemente a reconstruir su vida civil desde cero. Por si eso no fuera suficiente, aceptando con amargura que el precio real de salvar al multiverso fue perder irremediablemente su propia historia personal. Lo que le convierte en un completo fantasma para la sociedad que protege día a día.
La pérdida de la tía May y la madurez callejera
Para colmo de males, Peter no solamente fue olvidado: no tiene pariente vivo al cual recurrir. De modo que ya no es el adolescente que dependía por completo de la mentoría cercana o la inmensa fortuna tecnológica de Industrias Stark. La muerte de la tía May (Marisa Tomei) a manos del Duende Verde (Willem Dafoe) lo despojó de su último lazo familiar real. Lo que provoca, además, que Peter no solamente esté aislado porque ninguna de las personas que le conocieron fallecieron. A la vez, de toda posibilidad de conectar con su pasado, su vida y su identidad antes de su encuentro con Tony Stark (Robert Downey Jr.).
Un giro de los acontecimientos que llevó a Peter a tener que comenzar su vida desde cero. Sin recursos económicos, un mentor vivo que guíe sus pasos y viviendo de manera precaria en un pequeño, Peter evolucionó a un héroe distinto. En especial, porque la cinta comienza cuatro años después del hechizo de Strange y en un punto en que la vida del héroe arácnido está enfocada en su lado más heroico. Lo que le ha llevado a ser un hombre por completo nuevo. Pero, como lo saben los fanáticos del cómic, se trata de una imagen mucho más cercana y parecida a la del mundo de las viñetas que la anterior.
Otro punto esencial a recordar es que tanto el olvido masivo, como la muerte de Tía May convirtieron la identidad de Peter en un enigma. Como se recordará, Spider-Man: No Way Home comenzaba con el hecho de ser descubierto como héroe. Lo que complicó a niveles alarmantes su vida personal y, además, su futuro. Pero en Spider-Man: Brand New Day, el rostro que se esconde detrás de la máscara se convierte de nuevo en un oso que llevar para Peter Parker.
Aliados inesperados y las nuevas conexiones del UCM
Para Spider-Man: Brand New Day, el entorno habitual del héroe arácnido, se expande de forma notable. Eso, al incluir figuras verdaderamente clave del vasto universo cinematográfico de Marvel. Todas, que además, justifican por completo su nueva y caótica dinámica. El violento justiciero Frank Castle, cruzará inevitablemente caminos con Spider-Man tras los sangrientos eventos que este ha experimentado de forma totalmente aislada.
Por otro lado, el brillante científico Bruce Banner reaparece en su faceta investigadora. Pero también convirtiéndose en un Hulk sumamente salvaje e indomable bajo la premisa de no dar tregua ni descanso a su atribulado alter ego humano. Además, las agencias gubernamentales fuertemente armadas, tales como el temido Departamento de Control de Daños (DODC), siguen vigilando muy de cerca todos los incidentes metahumanos. Por lo que asumen un rol casi antagonista en la fiscalización de los vigilantes.
Estas peligrosas interacciones prometen colisionar con la solitaria vida de Peter, forzándolo a interactuar constantemente con facciones radicales que operan al margen de la ley. Todo un nuevo giro que brinda a Spider-Man: Brand New Day la oportunidad de profundizar en el héroe de Nueva York desde dimensiones por completo nuevas. Un regalo para fanáticos.
¿Y los villanos?
Spider-Man: Brand New Day presenta una amplia galería de antagonistas de corte callejero. El enemigo principal que regresa es El Escorpión (Mac Gargan), acompañado por Tombstone (Lonnie Lincoln). Como se recordará, el némesis principal de la cinta ya debutó en el Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel. El Escorpión lo hizo originalmente en la gran pantalla en Spider-Man: Homecoming (2017).

articles.title: You could be taking way better photos on your phone
articles.text:
Your smartphone photos can look way better. If you’re willing to put in a little extra work, use third party apps and spend a bit of time editing, it’s possible to take photos that — under the right circumstances — can rival dedicated digital cameras.
You could be taking way better photos on your phone
It takes a little more work, but phones can now legitimately rival point and shoot cameras.
I post a lot of smartphone photos online, and “How do I take better photos on my phone?” is a question I get practically every day. It makes sense. As the saying goes, “The best camera is the one you have on you,” and we practically always have our phones on us these days.
Over the last few years, smartphone camera sensors have gotten bigger, with better light gathering capabilities and higher resolutions. But even though the sensors have gotten bigger and better, the straight-out-of-camera quality through default camera apps hasn’t improved much, if at all. In some respects, smartphone photos have actually gotten worse — aesthetically, at least.
The reason driving this is what people generally use their smartphone cameras for. Smartphone cameras are mostly optimized for information transfer — sending photos of menus, signs, faces and objects that are clear and easy to see. This means phones will usually pull down highlights and pull up the shadows, creating a flatter image that makes it easier to see more information in the frame. But showing more information does not automatically make a photo better. In fact, much of our perception of aesthetics in a photo has to do with its ability to present depth. A photo with too much information in the shadows and highlights will appear washed out. Phones also introduce artifacts like over-sharpening and noise reduction to compensate for thier small sensors, which further contributes to the “muddy” smartphone camera look you’re used to seeing by now. This is less necessary now, but many smartphones still do it.
But that doesn’t mean phone cameras are bad. The sensors in modern smartphones have actually gotten so good, many of them can rival dedicated point-and-shoot options on the market today. Knowing how to utilize those sensors is the part most people don’t know how to do, and it really comes down to utilizing some third-party camera and editing apps.
The apps
There are plenty of apps available today that will give you an instantly “aesthetic” photo. Apps like Dazzcam and Hujicam try to emulate film aesthetics like light leaks and polaroid borders (and honestly, if that’s what you’re looking for, they do a fantastic job). There are also apps like Moment Pro Camera II and Halide that offer “Natural” and “Process Zero” modes, which apply far lighter processing than the default camera offers.
Those options are great if you want your pictures to look better instantly without needing to do any additional editing, but if you want the best possible photo, you’ll need to shoot RAW or DNG.
RAW files are a bundle of practically all the information your camera collects, with extremely minimal processing. In most cases, RAW photos won’t necessarily look better than photos straight from the default camera app right away, but that’s because the default camera app makes a lot of creative decisions for you. If you want the highest-quality photo, it’s best to make these creative decisions yourself.
There are tons of apps available that let you shoot RAW, but the apps I use frequently and that I recommend to other people are Moment Pro Camera II and Halide on iOS, and VWFNDR and Zerocam on Android.
I wouldn’t recommend shooting RAW on every photo you take on your phone. Your phone camera is, after all, optimized for what you are probably taking photos of every day. I generally shoot RAW when I see a nice landscape or city scene that I want to share, or if I’m trying to take a portrait of someone and don’t want all the automatic computational phone processing to apply. Really, I shoot RAW when I’m trying to take a photo for artistic purposes, not for informational purposes.
When you’re shooting, you’ll want to tap on your subject in the viewfinder to get the best possible exposure for it. If the rest of the image is a little bright, or a little dark, don’t worry too much. RAW photos retain a lot of information. I should note, though, that under extremely dark circumstances, RAW on smartphones won’t always be the best option. Physics is still physics, and sometimes it’s better to use the computational photography capabilities your phone offers, which mostly shine in low-light environments by stacking multiple frames to reduce noise.
You’ll notice that when you shoot in RAW, the apps will force you to stick to the native focal lengths your phone offers. That’s because RAW images are information straight off the sensor, and cropping applies processing. Photos from the main sensor will often be the best quality, since it usually has the biggest sensor on your phone, so I recommend shooting with it if you can. I do often shoot with the telephoto lens while traveling though, because sometimes you want a little more reach or a little more compression, and you can usually get good photos from that lens as well.
Editing
After you take your photos, you’re going to need to edit them. Most phones won’t show RAW images in the camera gallery, so in order to get them in an editing app, it’s best to use the share sheet and share directly to your editing app of choice. I suggest Snapseed, since it’s totally free and recently got a wonderful visual overhaul. If you’re an Adobe subscriber, Lightroom Mobile is also great, especially if you’re already used to Lightroom’s tools on your computer.
RAW photos don’t usually look great right away, and the magic of RAW is just how much you can tweak the files. Once I have the photo imported, I usually hit the auto button, just to see what the general boundaries are for the image. Auto mode tries to make everything a mid-tone, meaning it will pull down the highlights and pull up the shadows. This will already look better than straight-out-of-camera from your phone’s default camera app, because it isn’t applying noise reduction or sharpening, just highlight, shadow, contrast, and saturation tweaks, but it usually still needs more, or different, adjustments.
Once I see what auto mode wants to do, I’ll either edit from there, or hit the back button and edit myself. A good photo has a natural amount of contrast, with relatively deep shadows and bright highlights. You usually don’t want to go too hard on either of these things, and having a little bit of detail in both of these is usually preferred, but honestly, this is subjective. Occasionally, it’s preferable to crush the highlights and shadows completely, if you’re going for an ultra high-contrast look.
For color, RAW images are usually flatter than most people find pleasing, and you can fix this with either the saturation or vibrance sliders. I generally prefer vibrance. Saturation will increase the saturation of all colors in the image linearly, where vibrance is weighted, increasing saturation of flatter colors more than already-saturated colors. You can overdo this pretty easily, so I recommend having a light touch when it comes to saturation. You can also use white balance to color your image, and many people find a warmer white balance more pleasing, especially when taking photos outside.
Another color tool I love to use is the color mix, or selective editing tool. This allows you to tap on a portion of the image and change some of its values. In Snapseed, you can change the brightness, contrast, saturation, and structure. If you’re in Lightroom mobile, you’ll have access to selective hue shifts, which I use all the time. This allows you to shift a yellow tone towards more orange or green, or shift a blue tone more cyan or purple.
Most editing apps also include geometry or perspective tools. These tools allow you to adjust distortion, aspect, scale, and offset. If you don’t know what that means, try hitting the auto button in the geometry or perspective setting. You might be surprised how distorted your phone captured a scene compared to what it looks like in reality, but this is image-dependent. If you want to straighten lines in your photo, some editing apps offer a guided tool that allows you to manually add guidance lines to tell the program what lines should be straight in the image.
The tools you’ll want to use are going to depend heavily on what you want the image to convey. For example, when I’m doing architectural photography, I rely a lot more heavily on the perspective tools, because the aesthetic of the image is heavily dictated by its geometry. If I’m photographing a landscape, I’m more focused on tone and color. Not every scene needs to be tweaked with every tool, and how you edit comes down to personal taste. That taste can also take a while to develop, so study the photos you like and try to figure out how they were edited.
When you’re done with your edits, many editing apps like Snapseed and Lightroom Mobile also come with a handy tool to put a matte (or border) around your image. I think that photos look better with a white border, as it isolates the image for your eyes. You obviously don’t have to use this tool, but I really like it. Have some whimsy!
This process is a lot more work than just opening your camera app and snapping, but the results are worth it. I am continuously blown away by the quality of images I’m able to get off smartphones, and just how close they can be to a dedicated camera. If you don’t believe me, check out this video I did comparing RAW photos from the iPhone 17 Pro to the Leica M11.
Photography by David Imel / The Verge

articles.title: Coldcard Hardware Wallet Flaw Linked to $70 Million Bitcoin Theft in 41 Minutes
articles.text:
An attacker drained 1,196 Bitcoin addresses in 41 minutes on July 30, taking 1,082.65 BTC worth about $70.2 million at the time. Galaxy Research mapped the sweep and tied it to a firmware flaw in Coldcard, the Bitcoin-only hardware wallet made by Canadian firm Coinkite.
A March 2021 firmware integration error routed seed generation to a deterministic software pseudorandom number generator (PRNG) instead of the STM32 hardware random number generator (RNG).
Block says an attacker who can determine or sufficiently constrain the device UID, timer state, and prior RNG-call history can reproduce candidate output streams offline without accessing the device. Candidate seeds can then be checked by deriving their addresses and comparing them with public blockchain data.
Coinkite shipped emergency firmware for every affected model and release track on July 31, but installing it does not repair an existing seed. Coinkite tells owners with exposed seeds to generate a new one on patched firmware and move their coins.
Restoring the old seed to updated firmware or another wallet carries the weakness forward. No public report has reconstructed a victim's seed and matched it to a drained address.
Block traced the fault to Coldcard's production config, which defines MICROPY_HW_ENABLE_RNG as zero because Coinkite supplies its own hardware-RNG wrapper. The libngu library checked whether the macro existed rather than whether it was enabled, binding the build to MicroPython's Yasmarang fallback. The MicroPython fallback was initialized from the chip's unique ID and timer registers and collected no fresh entropy after initialization.
Coinkite estimates effective entropy at roughly 40 bits on the Mk3 and about 72 bits on the Mk4, Mk5 and Q, against 128 bits for a 12-word BIP-39 seed. Block does not give one practical figure. It sets conditional ceilings below 240.7 and 273.3 and warns that the latter is not equivalent to 73-bit cryptographic security. It published no brute-force benchmark.
| Image Source: Galaxy Research | 
The later-model reseed raises the number of candidates, but Block says practical cost depends on available UID information, boot timing, prior RNG calls and derivation cost.
Exposure depends on the firmware running when the seed was created, not the version installed now:
- Mk2 and Mk3: Coinkite lists Mk3 versions 4.0.1 through 4.1.9, fixed in 4.2.0, and does not name Mk2. Block places both Mk2 and Mk3 versions 4.0.0 through 4.1.9 on the vulnerable path.
- Mk4 and Mk5: anything before 5.6.0.
- Q: anything before 1.5.0Q.
- Edge builds: before 6.6.0X for Mk4 and Mk5, before 6.6.0QX for Q.
Coinkite says a seed built with at least 50 fair, independent, private dice rolls is not at risk from this bug alone. If the number or privacy of the rolls is uncertain, Coinkite says to migrate. A strong, unique BIP-39 passphrase creates a separate wallet the seed words cannot reach on their own, but the company still recommends replacing the seed.
Multisig helps only when the quorum is not built entirely from affected devices. TAPSIGNER, OPENDIME and SATSCARD use different codebases and are unaffected.
No one has named the attacker. Galaxy, which mapped the 1,196-address sweep, said it found no other Bitcoin transactions in the previous 30 days with the same 30 sat/vB, no-change signature.
It warned that the pattern identifies the operator, not the theft, because a sweep "looks the same as if a coin owner chose to move coins."
The disclosure follows Coinspect's Ill Bloom research in early July, a separate weak-PRNG flaw in older software wallets tied to more than $5 million drained from addresses across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Rootstock and Polygon since May.

articles.title: Le vélo électrique de ville Moustache Samedi 28.1 est proposé à 1 349 euros en version reconditionnée
articles.text:
Rouler à vélo au quotidien en ville demande de choisir un modèle adapté à ses trajets, suffisamment confortable et fiable pour accompagner les déplacements de tous les jours. Un vélo à assistance électrique (VAE) apparaît comme une solution toute trouvée, mais le principal frein reste le prix, souvent élevé. Se tourner vers le marché du reconditionné peut alors être une bonne alternative pour profiter d’un vélo électrique performant à un tarif plus accessible, tout en donnant une seconde vie à un modèle qui a encore beaucoup à offrir.
Le vélo électrique Moustache Samedi 28.1 avec cadre fermé est normalement vendu 2 099 € en neuf. Il est en ce moment proposé au prix de 1 349 € sur le site d’Upway.
Le modèle avec cadre ouvert, que l’on a pu tester sur Numerama, est également proposé en reconditionné sur Upway au prix de 1 599 € au lieu de 2 299 € normalement.
C’est quoi, ce vélo de ville de Moustache ?
Le Moustache Samedi 28.1 reprend les codes qui font l’identité du constructeur, avec son cadre élégant, son guidon en forme de M et ses grandes roues de 28 pouces équipées de pneus adaptés à la ville. La position de conduite, naturellement droite, privilégie le confort plutôt que la performance et permet de pédaler sans trop solliciter le dos. Le vélo profite également d’une suspension avant Suntour, et de freins à disques hydrauliques puissants.
Pour la motorisation, Moustache a opté pour un moteur Bosch Active Line de 250 W et 40 Nm, associé à une batterie amovible de 400 Wh. L’assistance permet de se déplacer facilement en ville, notamment dans les faux plats et les montées, même si elle se montre moins vigoureuse que celle des moteurs Bosch plus haut de gamme. Heureusement, le Samedi 28.1 dispose d’un dérailleur à 9 vitesses, qui permet d’adapter facilement son effort aux différents types de parcours.
À ce prix, le Moustache Samedi 28.1 est-il une bonne affaire ?
Ces deux VAE de ville de Moustache sont d’excellentes affaires à ce prix. Le modèle avec cadre fermé, vendu 1 349 €, a parcouru 1 130 km depuis 2022, tandis que le modèle avec cadre ouvert vendu moins de 1 600 € n’a parcouru que 95 km depuis son achat en 2023. Ces Moustache Samedi 28.1 viennent avec un porte-bagage arrière en aluminium, des garde-boue en aluminium avant et arrière, et des éclairages.
Niveau autonomie, en mode Turbo, la batterie permet de parcourir environ 40 kilomètres en usage urbain, tandis que les modes Tour et Eco permettent de dépasser les 60 kilomètres dans de bonnes conditions.

articles.title: Windows 11 : la mise à jour d’août va faire le plein de nouveautés, voici ce qu’il faut retenir
articles.text:
La mise à jour du mois d’août sera riche en nouveautés. Microsoft vient en effet de déployer la mise à jour KB5101684 pour Windows 11, une version optionnelle ayant été proposée en avant-première à la fin de ce mois de juillet.
Avec environ 5 Go au téléchargement, les changements qu’elle apporte sont assez importants avec plusieurs améliorations concernant les performances du système d’exploitation.
Toutes les nouveautés qu’elle introduit seront déployées à grande échelle avec le prochain Patch Tuesday, dont le déploiement est en principe prévu pour le mardi 11 août 2026. Voici tout ce qu’il faut en retenir.
Des améliorations majeures pour l’Explorateur de fichiers
Avec cette mise à jour, Microsoft a mis le paquet pour optimiser l’Explorateur de fichiers de Windows 11. Parmi ces nouveautés, qui visent à améliorer l’utilisation quotidienne du centre névralgique de Windows, Microsoft a modifié le système unitaire utilisé pour afficher la taille des fichiers. Les tailles ne sont désormais plus systématiquement affichées en Ko, mais avec l’unité la plus appropriée, à savoir des Mo et de Go, facilitant ainsi la lecture de l’occupation du stockage par les différents éléments présents sur votre PC.
Autre nouveauté intéressante, il est à présent possible d’ouvrir un dossier dans un nouvel onglet, en utilisant simplement le clic du milieu, sur la molette de votre souris par exemple.
Microsoft indique également avoir corrigé un bug qui générait un flash gris au chargement ou lors du défilement de contenu sur la page d’Accueil de l’Explorateur de fichiers.
La recherche dans Windows devient enfin intelligente
Cette mise à jour du mois d’août s’attaque également à l’un des plus grands défauts de Windows 11 : son piètre moteur de recherche. Les ingénieurs de Microsoft se sont penchés sur la question et ont ainsi réalisé plusieurs améliorations qui devraient enfin lui permettre d’être suffisamment efficace pour être utile.
La recherche Windows devient intelligente et peut à présent gérer vos fautes de frappe. Concrètement, cela signifie que le moteur de recherche pourra trouver des applications ou des paramètres même si vous glissez une coquille dans votre requête.
Par ailleurs, les résultats proposés devraient être plus pertinents qu’à l’accoutumée et devraient vous amener exactement là où vous souhaitez aller, notamment si vous cherchez à accéder à certains paramètres du système d’exploitation.
Plus de stabilité et des performances en hausse
Plus globalement, les efforts des développeurs de Microsoft se sont portés sur l’optimisation de certains éléments du système parfois un peu capricieux. Microsoft a corrigé un bug qui empêchait la mémorisation des préférences au sein du menu Démarrer, qui par la même occasion a gagné en fluidité, en particulier sur les machines à la configuration modeste.
Les ralentissements subis par le système et l’utilisation trop importante de mémoire ont en partie été corrigés, tandis que Microsoft a multiplié les efforts pour rendre le processus de connexion plus efficace, avec un menu Démarrer et une barre des tâches bien plus réactifs après le démarrage du PC.
Isolation de la voix, nouvelles options du trackpad et plus encore
Pour le reste, Microsoft annonce avoir ajouté l’isolation vocale à son module d’accès vocal. En filtrant les bruits ambiants, et en supprimant les interférences provenant d’autres haut-parleurs, l’accès vocal devrait mieux reconnaître votre voix et donc s’avérer plus efficace.
Microsoft a également profité de cette mise à jour pour harmoniser les badges de notification sur la barre des tâches. Plutôt que de s’afficher en rouge comme c’est le cas actuellement, ils adopteront désormais la couleur d’accentuation que vous avez sélectionnée dans les paramètres de personnalisation de Windows 11. À noter aussi que Microsoft a simplifié son utilisation des widgets sur l’écran de verrouillage. À présent, seul le widget météo sera affiché sur l’écran de verrouillage par défaut.
Enfin, la firme de Redmond a introduit de nouvelles commandes gestuelles pour les pavés tactiles de précision. Disponibles en se rendant dans les Paramètres > Bluetooth et appareils > Pavé tactile, ces nouveaux paramètres vous permettront d’ajuster la vitesse de base pour les mouvements de défilement, et vous permettra par la même occasion d’activer une option pour faire défiler le contenu plus rapidement au fur et à mesure que vous scrollez sur répétez le geste pour faire défiler le contenu sur le trackpad.
