The OG reading app just got a big update
Plus, in this week’s Installer: Spider-Man is back again, a cozy game worth trying, Elon roasts, and much more.
This week, I’ve been reading about microwave sounds and Meta glasses and Alex vs. Alix, testing the Logitech Alto Keys K98M to see if I’m ready for the mechanical keyboard life, digging into the history of the first chatbot, clearing space on my desk for a Bob Ross deskmat, doing a full Ted Lasso rewatch ahead of the new season next week, finally getting into Cyberpunk 2077 now that it’s so cheap, cackling and nodding at this Adobe hate post, and upgrading my home camera setup with the truly enormous Elgato Prompter XL.
Also, I have some personal news: I’m having a baby! (If your response to this is, Didn’t you just have like 37 other babies, yes, yes I did. Pray for me.) I’m planning to be out from about mid-August to the beginning of October, but I’m also in could-happen-anytime land now. So if I’m suddenly gone, that’s why! Just like last year, my colleague Jay Peters will be taking over Installer while I’m out, and just like last year, he’s going to be great.
But for now, I’m still here! I also have for you a new superhero movie, a new take on an old game, some great Musk-related comedy, and much more. Let’s do it.
(As always, the best part of Installer is your ideas and tips. What are you watching / reading / playing / listening to / putting in a blender this week? Tell me everything: installer@theverge.com. And if you know someone else who might enjoy Installer, forward it to them and tell them to subscribe here.)
The Drop
- Spider-Man: Brand New Day. The Tom Holland Spidey era just never seems to miss. It’s pretty impressive to pull off a more or less full story reboot while keeping all the same actors and characters, but by all accounts this one pulls it off. Since I still can’t get IMAX Odyssey tickets, this one’s at the top of my to-watch list.
- Pastebot 3. Missed this one last week! Great clipboard managers are right up there with launchers and text expanders in the “how did I ever use a computer without this” category, and Pastebot is one of the Mac’s best. The new version has smart organization options, support for all kinds of media, and much more. The kind of app you’ll find new uses for… forever.
- President Curtis. I was going to describe this as “basically a Rick and Morty spinoff” before I realized it’s actually a Rick and Morty spinoff. Perhaps unsurprisingly, people seem to either love it or hate it. I think most of us would agree R&M is not what it once was, but the idea of throwing all its chaotic energy into the US government does pay off at least a few times. And it’s not not political commentary, you know?
- “Why Is So Much AI Tech Useless?” Two of my favorite people on the internet — Joanna Stern and Hasan Minhaj — go deep on where AI is, and isn’t, actually good and useful in our lives. Minhaj’s complete disbelief at all these overhyped products just gives me life.
- Halo: Campaign Evolved. Confession: I was always terrible at Halo, and I’ve always been unfairly mad at the series because of it. The new remake appears to be a mediocre game (with terrible dialogue) but great nostalgia bait, and that might be enough for a lot of people looking to get Master Chief back into their lives.
- Leafy Corner. This game exists somewhere on the spectrum between Animal Crossing and RollerCoaster Tycoon, and I mean both as a compliment. It’s a quiet, cozy game, but also something of a management sim, all in the confines of a plant shop. Adorable.
- Spotify Running Mode. I actually think Spotify’s last take on running, with adaptive tempos and generative beats, was both cooler and a more interesting take on AI. But Spotify’s prompted playlists have generally been pretty good, and I appreciate having the timing updates built in instead of having some other app constantly ducking my music to tell me I’m too slow.
- “Elon’s Epic Ego Explained.” Nobody does topical comedy like Josh Johnson, and this is my favorite of his recent sets. It’s not just 45 minutes of making fun of Musk — it’s also about The Odyssey and a bunch of other things — but it’s both ruthless and right about the world’s richest man.
- The SwitchBot Battery Circulator Fan 2 Pro. My colleague Thomas Ricker has successfully convinced me that SwitchBot’s fans are worth a look over the “whatever’s on the shelf at Target” models I’ve been buying for years. This new $120 model is quiet and powerful, charges over USB-C, and is going to live on my patio the rest of the summer.
I buried the lede here: The biggest new thing of the week, at least in my book, is Instapaper 10. Instapaper is one of the original read-later apps, and has continued to be among the best on the market. After some weird ownership stuff over the years, Instapaper has been in the hands of Brian Donohue, who has been steadily improving the service in lots of ways. This week’s launch comes with a really nice redesign, a way better web app, and a lot of helpful organization and reading tools. I’ve been testing it, and I think it’s back to being my go-to recommendation for reading apps. (For power users I still think Readwise is the move.)
With the new app out, I asked Brian to share his homescreen with us — I wanted to see how he organized his stuff, and if he might be working on even more cool stuff. Turns out he is! Here’s his homescreen, plus some info on the apps he uses and why:
The phone: iPhone 16 Pro. I almost always purchase iPhones every other generation. Maybe a foldable this year?
The wallpaper: My daughter, as a reminder that my apps must be good otherwise she will not have food on the table.
The apps: Safari, Google Calendar, Emerald, Google Maps, Weather, Photos, Instapaper, Kobo Books, Reddit, 1Password, Google Authenticator, Slack, Google Docs, Google Sheets, ForeFlight, Flight Circle, Claude, Linear, Phone, Sunflower, Messages, Spotify.
I’ll start with the ones not yet in the App Store: Emerald and Sunflower.
Emerald is a Markdown editor I’m working on that solves two personal pain points: native iOS / macOS client, and collaboration on markdown files. I have been a big Obsidian user the past two years, but it’s been failing me in those areas. I’ve been writing with Emerald exclusively for the past few months and it’s almost ready for beta testing. Waitlist in the link.
Sunflower is a new email client from Bobby Goodlatte and friends. It’s beautifully designed and has some tasteful AI features, like summarizing your inbox, chatting with your email, and an Autopilot feature which seems to be perpetually “Coming Soon.” I’ve been trying a few clients in the “AI email” space like Extra, and an autopilot tool called Cora, which didn’t stick.
Instapaper’s big launch this week included a new home screen widget. It fits nicely in the widget stack alongside the Apple News, Stocks, and Weather widgets.
Additionally, you have many of the usual suspects. I am doing a huge amount of my work with Claude and Linear these days, both of which have fantastic iOS apps.
I also asked Brian to share a few things he’s into right now. Here’s what he sent back:
- I’ve always been inspired by creative builders, and two come to mind right now. The first is Andrew Jones, who has been building free & open-source alternatives to paid software (e.g. Granola, Wispr Flow) — fingers crossed Instapaper is not next. The second is Q, a designer who has been building small, single-purpose websites for himself that I find inspiring. It almost reminds me of a purer, distant version of the Internet, where you built a bunch of Geocities pages for fun and without expectations of fame and fortune.
- Hyper Mesh. Q has been exploring image reveal animations, and built a tool to tweak presets on the initial mask and the animation that reveals the image.
- SVG Star Editor. Create a star from different settings and export to SVG.
- Chess Moves. Q is learning how to play chess with his girlfriend and made this tutorial website as a companion tool.
Crowdsourced
Here’s what the Installer community is into this week. I want to know what you’re into right now as well! Email installer@theverge.com or message me on Signal — @davidpierce.11 — with your recommendations for anything and everything, and we’ll feature some of our favorites here every week. For even more great recommendations, check out the replies to this post on Threads and this post on Bluesky.
“I am hopelessly hooked on the game Murdoku. It’s free online, or you can play old school through books. It’s a logic game where you solve crimes by process of elimination.” — Kurt
“I’ve been loving Paradiso for finding movie showtimes. Not only does it alert you when something on your Letterboxd watchlist is playing near you, it also beats Fandango or other apps for simply browsing first run showtimes.” — Mike
“My friend recently ordered a Galaxy Z Fold 8 and I had to introduce them to Good Lock.” — B
“I love Anker stuff and tend to choose it over everything else. But I have the Anker 3-in-1 travel charger and… this ESR one (a brand I hadn’t really heard of) is the better product in every way. The Apple Watch charger is in a better place, it’s thinner, and the cooling fan works better. I can’t vouch for long-term reliability yet, but I have one by my bedside and one in my travel bag!” — Peter
“Finally switched from a mess of read-it-later apps to a second brain with Obsidian + Claude, inspired by Karpathy’s LLM Wiki concept. Hoping this setup is the one that actually sticks…” — Kartik
“I use Readwise Reader for all my newsletters. It has unique email addresses to either add newsletters to your library or RSS feed. I love keeping all my things to read all in the same app, read later, newsletters, pdfs…” — Rich
“HIGHLY recommend the movie Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender. It’s a crime and shame that Paramount isn’t putting this into more theaters, AND that the movie was leaked on X earlier this year. Amazing film with all-time stunning visuals that honestly left me angry I was watching it on TV at home. Deserves bettering than being dumped on Paramount Plus.” — Nolan
“Watching the restored version of Lawrence of Arabia. Peter O’Toole’s blue eyes are dreamy.” — SaltedPork
Signing off
The coolest internet experience I had this week was scrolling through the Everything Machine, a deep and detailed breakdown of how your phone works. It’s only the first chapter of what I hope will be a very long exploration of how smartphones changed everything, and I love the way it seems to interact with your phone as you scroll. Our phones are such a “This is water” thing in our lives now, and I really enjoy anything that makes me pay a little more attention to the object, the cultural force, and the economic engine that takes up so much of my life. Highly recommend taking a scroll.
See you next week!

articles.title: Honda fecha parceria com QuantumScape para desenvolver baterias de estado sólido
articles.text:
A Honda anunciou em junho de 2026 uma parceria com a QuantumScape, empresa americana de desenvolvimento de baterias sediada em San Jose, Califórnia, para pesquisar e desenvolver baterias de estado sólido e as técnicas de fabricação associadas. De acordo com a engadget, o acordo foi firmado poucos meses depois de a Honda cancelar o lançamento norte-americano de três modelos elétricos — o Honda 0 SUV, o Honda 0 Saloon e o Acura RSX —, movimento que coincidiu com o primeiro prejuízo financeiro anual da empresa em quase 75 anos.
Em comunicado divulgado pela QuantumScape, o diretor de operações do Centro de Excelência em Pesquisa da Honda R&D, Atsushi Ogawa, afirmou que a plataforma de tecnologia de estado sólido da empresa “demonstrou vantagens convincentes e únicas” durante um estudo técnico e que a parceria poderia “agregar valor em uma série de aplicações”. A QuantumScape havia firmado acordo semelhante no ano anterior com a PowerCo SE, empresa de baterias do grupo Volkswagen. Além dos veículos elétricos, a QuantumScape posiciona suas baterias de estado sólido como solução para mercados emergentes com alta demanda energética, como data centers, drones e robótica. A Honda tem como meta atingir a neutralidade de carbono até 2050 e escalar sua produção de veículos elétricos para 100% das vendas até 2040.
Como funciona a tecnologia de estado sólido
Nas baterias de íons de lítio usadas pela maioria dos veículos elétricos atuais, os eletrólitos, responsáveis por transportar elétrons carregados positivamente entre os terminais positivo (cátodo) e negativo (ânodo), são formados por soluções líquidas de sais de lítio dissolvidos em solventes orgânicos. As baterias de estado sólido substituem esses líquidos por eletrólitos sólidos, como óxidos, sulfetos, sais poliméricos ou polímeros em gel. Essa mudança também permite substituir os ânodos de carbono ou silício por alternativas com maior densidade energética, como o lítio metálico.
De acordo com a QuantumScape, um veículo elétrico equipado com uma de suas células poderia ampliar sua autonomia de 350 milhas para uma faixa entre 400 e 500 milhas. A Honda estimou que uma bateria de estado sólido poderia atingir entre 80% e 90% de carga em questão de minutos. Executivos da Honda também afirmaram que a tecnologia poderia dobrar a autonomia estendida dos modelos elétricos atuais até o fim da década.
Os eletrólitos sólidos eliminam o risco de vazamento, não são inflamáveis e são menos suscetíveis à deterioração por reações químicas adicionais. As baterias de estado sólido também operam em temperaturas extremas. A tecnologia ainda poderia eliminar a necessidade de ânodos de grafite, reduzindo a dependência do mercado de veículos elétricos de fornecedores chineses desse material.
Apesar dessas vantagens, nenhum fabricante lançou até agora um veículo elétrico movido inteiramente por baterias de estado sólido para o mercado consumidor. A principal barreira tem sido a escalabilidade diante dos custos elevados.
A Honda iniciou sua trajetória em baterias de estado sólido em 2024, quando anunciou a intenção de produzir protótipos em sua instalação em Sakura City, no Japão. A parceria com a QuantumScape prevê o uso da instalação Eagle Line, recentemente inaugurada pela empresa americana, para produzir as células QSE-5 — sem ânodo e com lítio metálico —, que estrearam em um protótipo de motocicleta Ducati V21L no outono passado. A empresa espera lançar um veículo elétrico de estado sólido até o fim da década.
Beatriz Campos é jornalista formada pela Universidade São Judas Tadeu e jornalista do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Cómo calibrar tus mandos de PS5, Xbox y PC para evitar los movimientos fantasma
articles.text:
Si eres o has sido un jugador habitual de consolas clásicas o actuales, en alguna ocasión te habrás encontrado con que tu mando de juego se rebela. Es decir, que el personaje empieza a moverse por sí mismo o los movimientos no son tan precisos. Ocurre cuando el mando acumula horas de juego y ha sufrido cierto desgaste. Y se conoce como stick drift o joystick drift, que podríamos traducir como movimientos involuntarios o movimientos fantasma. Para solucionarlo, puedes hacer varias cosas. La más eficaz consiste en cambiar de mando. Pero si está fuera de garantía, te costará dinero. Y si el problema no es muy grave, puede que logres solventarlo si pruebas a calibrar los mandos. ¿Cómo se hace? Con herramientas como DriftGuard.
Problemas con los mandos de juego los hemos tenido prácticamente todos los jugadores desde que el mundo es mundo. Sin embargo, estos problemas han ido a más a medida que los mandos se volvían más complejos. Los mandos clásicos eran básicamente analógicos. Pero las generaciones más recientes de PlayStation, Xbox y Nintendo incorporan toda clase de sensores que ofrecen una experiencia de juego superior. Pero que, con el paso del tiempo, acaban por dar problemas.
Así que si experimentas movimientos fantasma en tu consola de juego u ordenador, es decir, que el personaje y/o la cámara se mueven sin que tú estés tocando los joysticks o la cruceta, y ya has probado a actualizar el mando y la consola, a cargar la batería o a apagar y a reiniciar, siempre te quedará la tarea de calibrar tus mandos. No hace milagros, pero puede que te evite tener que pasar por caja y comprar un nuevo mando.
Qué es DriftGuard y para qué sirve
DriftGuard es una herramienta de mantenimiento para mandos de juego que te permite probar, calibrar y ajustar esos mandos o controladores. Gratuita y de código abierto, entre sus particularidades destaca que graba la calibración directamente en la memoria del mando. El equipo de personas detrás de este proyecto advierte que “DriftGuard no puede solucionar los problemas graves de stick drift o movimientos involuntarios, pero puede ayudarte a calibrar tu mando para mejorar tu experiencia de juego, tanto antes como después de sustituir los joysticks analógicos”.
Para usar DriftGuard tienes tres opciones. Las tres compatibles con la mayoría de mandos del mercado, especialmente los mandos oficiales de PlayStation, Xbox y Nintendo, además de los mandos SCUF Instinct Pro. La más recomendable es la versión online, ya que no requiere instalar nada. Tan solo tener un navegador compatible con Chromium. Es decir, Chrome, Edge, Opera, Vivaldi, Brave y muchos otros. No requiere registro y es gratuito.
La segunda versión recomendada es la app de DriftGuard para Android. Gratuita con publicidad y con opciones de compra en la propia aplicación, puedes descargarla desde Google Play. “Conecta tu mando compatible de PlayStation o Xbox mediante USB, prueba el movimiento de los joysticks analógicos en tiempo real, detecta la deriva de los joysticks y utiliza herramientas de calibración diseñadas para reducir la deriva leve del mando y mejorar la precisión”.
Y, en tercer lugar, DriftGuard para Windows, disponible en Steam. En el momento de escribir esto, la app se encuentra etiquetada como software con acceso anticipado. Y tiene un coste de 33,99 €, que sirve para sufragar el proyecto. Recordemos que la versión online es gratuita.
Qué es el ‘stick drift’ o movimiento involuntario
Si acostumbras a utilizar mandos de juego para jugar, habrás oído hablar del joystick drift, stick drift o simplemente drift. Ya sea porque lo has experimentado tú mismo o porque has leído u oído hablar de ello. Es un problema que se ha agudizado especialmente en las dos últimas generaciones de las consolas de Sony, PlayStation 4 y PlayStation 5. Y con la PS5 hubo polémica porque los mandos no eran baratos y venían con ese problema de fábrica. Pero Microsoft y Nintendo tampoco se libran. Los mandos de la Nintendo Switch también daban problemas de movimientos involuntarios a algunos usuarios.
Y con los mandos de Xbox 360, Xbox One y Xbox Series sucede más de lo mismo. Es más. Una de las ventajas que ofrece DriftGuard es que es, según sus creadores, “la única herramienta que puede calibrar” los mandos de Microsoft. Y la única compatible con calibración para SCUF Instinct Pro.
Volviendo al tema. El drift o stick drift se produce cuando el potenciómetro, un sensor del joystick, deja de leer correctamente la posición del stick. Y esto provoca que el mando envíe señales erróneas aunque el mando esté quieto sobre la mesa. El resultado es que el personaje se mueve. O lo hace la cámara. O bien el cursor o menú se desplazan solos. Esto es un gran problema, especialmente en juegos en los que la precisión es importante. Que, básicamente, son la gran mayoría.
¿Qué provoca los movimientos involuntarios o movimientos fantasma? Una causa puede ser la suciedad y el polvo. Es inevitable que, con el paso del tiempo, el mando acumule algo más que sudor y lágrimas. A esto se le suma el desgaste del propio sensor. Y el trajín que le des al mando. Caídas, lanzamientos voluntarios o involuntarios, movimientos bruscos… Si a toda esta combinación le sumas que algunos mandos se fabrican con materiales, digamos, más propensos al desgaste, resulta inevitable que tu mando DualSense de PS5, DualShock de PS4, Xbox One, Xbox Series o Nintendo Pro acaben por mostrar movimientos involuntarios.
Mandos compatibles con DriftGuard
Otra de las particularidades de DriftGuard es que, a diferencia de otras herramientas tan especializadas, ofrece compatibilidad con la mayoría de mandos actuales o relativamente recientes. Solo tienes que conectar el mando vía USB al ordenador o dispositivo USB con DrifGuard y lo detectará. La lista completa de controladores compatibles es la siguiente:
- Sony DualSense para PlayStation 5
- Sony DualSense Edge para PlayStation 5
- Sony PlayStation Access Controller para PlayStation 5
- Sony PlayStation VR2 Sense Controller para PlayStation 5
- Scuf Reflex para PlayStation 5
- Sony DualShock 4 para PlayStation 4
- Sony DualShock 3 para PlayStation 3
- Microsoft Xbox Wireless Controller para Xbox Series S/X
- Microsoft Xbox Wireless Controller para Xbox One
- Microsoft Xbox 360 Wired Controller
- Microsoft Xbox 360 Wireless Controller
- Microsoft Xbox Elite Wireless Controller
- Microsoft Xbox Elite Wireless Controller Series 2
- SCUF Instinct Pro para Xbox
- Nintendo Switch Pro para Nintendo Switch
- Nintendo Joy-Con para Nintendo Switch (izquierdo y derecho)
Cómo funciona DriftGuard
DriftGuard lo pone increíblemente fácil. Los pasos a seguir para calibrar tus mandos con esta herramienta son asumibles por cualquiera. Solo tienes que elegir qué mando vas a calibrar, encender el mando y conectarlo al ordenador. A poder ser con cable USB. La herramienta lo detectará y ya podrás empezar la tarea de calibración pulsando el botón Start. Luego sigue las instrucciones que verás en pantalla. Y con un poco de suerte, tu mando funcionará como el primer día. Por defecto, la app está configurada en modo simple. Pero tiene un modo avanzado para los más experimentados.
- Abre DriftGuard en tu navegador.
- Elige la consola del mando que vas a calibrar: PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo u Other.
- Conecta el mando al PC o Mac. Vía Bluetooth o por USB.
- Haz clic en Click Here to connect. Al lado de Calibration.
- Tendrás que dar permiso al navegador para usar el mando.
- Ahora haz clic en Start para empezar las pruebas.
- Te pedirá que muevas los joysticks. Verás el análisis en tiempo real.
- Cuando acabe, te dará un diagnóstico.
- Puedes repetir la calibración pulsando en Retry.
- O guardar los cambios con Save.
- O deshacer los cambios con Restore.
DriftGuard también tiene una herramienta para probar el mando. Así podrás asegurarte de que el problema que has detectado es real o el mando funciona correctamente y fue algo puntual. O simplemente comprobar la precisión del mando. Y todo sin abrir ni desmontar el mando y desde el navegador web. Sin instalar nada en tu PC o Mac. Y gratis si empleas la app web.
Cuando ocurre un problema de drift o movimientos fantasma, en el peor de los casos, tienes que cambiar los sensores internos del joystick. Así que no te quedará otra que acudir a una tienda de reparaciones o comprar un mando nuevo. Sin embargo, antes de llegar a ello, probar DriftGuard te llevará unos pocos minutos y tal vez logres alargar la vida útil de tu mando de PlayStation, Xbox o Nintendo.

articles.title: Hijacked Hotel Wi-Fi Pushes Fake Updates to Deliver Surveillance Malware
articles.text:
A fake browser update served over hijacked hotel Wi-Fi has been used to deliver CornFlake, a remote access trojan (RAT) that can capture webcam images, microphone audio, and keystrokes, Microsoft said in its latest report.
Researchers track the operation as CaptiveCrunch and attribute it to Storm-2945. It assesses Storm-2945 to be an operational sub-cluster of Midnight Blizzard, also known as APT29 and Cozy Bear. The U.S. and U.K. governments attribute the broader actor to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR).
On the compromised networks ReliaQuest investigated, the captive portal gateway also served as the DNS resolver assigned to connected devices. Administrative control of that gateway let the attackers forge Domain Name System (DNS) answers and redirect the resulting traffic. They could then redirect a laptop's automatic connectivity check to a fake browser or operating system update.
Some pages use ClickFix instructions that tell victims to open a terminal or another Windows utility and run an attacker-supplied command. The gateway controls where the user is sent, but it does not silently infect the endpoint. The victim still has to download or execute the payload.
Microsoft has observed the traffic manipulation since early May across hospitality networks in several countries, but it has not named a hotel, venue, or captive portal vendor. ReliaQuest recommends an always-on, full-tunnel virtual private network (VPN), which sends DNS queries through corporate resolvers before the venue's gateway can answer them.
Researchers advise travelers to use private connections and reject software updates, certificates, browser updates, troubleshooting tools, or security utilities offered through captive portals.
Since July 16, some CaptiveCrunch landing pages have redirected guests into Microsoft's device code authentication flow. Entering the attacker-supplied code on Microsoft's legitimate sign-in page can grant the attacker-controlled session multi-factor authentication (MFA)-satisfied access. Microsoft recommends blocking the flow through Conditional Access wherever it is not needed.
CornFlake, a Go-based implant, copies itself to %APPDATA%\svchost32\svchost32.exe and registers the svchost32 service under the display name Cloud Sync Service. A fake progress window holds the victim's attention while this happens.
Microsoft's analysis says the implant can take idle-triggered screenshots, record clipboard contents with the active window title, steal browser cookies and saved passwords, including cookies protected by Chrome App-Bound Encryption, scan removable media, and open a remote shell. It also uses a Registry Run key and a scheduled task, while a watchdog restores any persistence mechanism defenders remove.
Researchers also identified ChocoShell, an in-memory PowerShell stealer. It collects Microsoft 365 and Azure Active Directory access and refresh tokens, plus Web Account Manager (WAM) tokens, from .tbres files in the Token Broker cache. The stolen tokens can enable session replay without a browser cookie.
The reports document active redirection and malware delivery, but do not quantify their reach or conversion. Without counts of successful executions, device-code approvals, or stolen accounts, the public record does not show how often a redirect became a compromise.
Microsoft found common equipment and management systems across the affected networks, which it says could reflect access to shared services within portions of the captive portal ecosystem. If so, the compromises may not have been isolated to individual venues. Microsoft has not named any affected provider.
ReliaQuest documented the same Microsoft-impersonating domains and overlapping infrastructure eight days earlier. It said the tradecraft resembled APT28, the GRU unit also called Fancy Bear and Forest Blizzard, but stopped short of attribution because the assessment rests on TTP overlap rather than direct technical linkage.
Microsoft acknowledges the similarity to the Forest Blizzard router hijacking it disclosed in April while attributing CaptiveCrunch to Storm-2945.
The U.K. National Cyber Security Centre and its international partners assess that APT29 is almost certainly part of Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service. That government attribution covers the broader APT29 group. The CaptiveCrunch-to-Storm-2945 link remains Microsoft's assessment. No separate public technical report has independently corroborated it.
The initial compromise vector remains under investigation. ReliaQuest assesses with low-to-medium confidence that a combination of exposed management interfaces and weak or reused administrator credentials may have provided access, but said visibility constraints prevented confirmation.

articles.title: Sauron contre le Balrog, Spider-Man contre Hulk, il y a de la bagarre dans le récap pop culture de la semaine
articles.text:
Les Anneaux de Pouvoir saison 3 : pourquoi le combat monumental de Sauron et le Balrog est fort surprenant
- Un clip promo de la saison 3 de Les Anneaux de Pouvoir dévoile un duel entre Sauron et le Fléau de Durin.
- Sauron y oppose la Couronne de Fer de Morgoth aux assauts du Balrog.
- La série légitime ce face‑à‑face en s’appuyant sur une ligne des appendices de Tolkien suggérant que le Balrog a pu être « déjà réveillé par la malice de Sauron ».
Que signifie la scène post-générique de Spider-Man: Brand New Day ?
- Spider-Man: Brand New Day se contente d’une unique scène post-générique sobre et sans fan-service, conçue comme un « passage de témoin » plutôt que comme un coup d’éclat.
- Tom Holland n’apparaît pas officiellement au casting d’Avengers: Doomsday.
- La scène révèle que le spider-tracker localise Peter non pas sur Terre mais perdu dans le vide spatial, pavant la voie à son insertion directe dans Battleworld et la suite menant à Secret Wars.
Spider-Man: Brand New Day : on sait enfin pourquoi Hulk est absent d’Avengers: Doomsday
- Dans Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Marvel ramène le « Savage Hulk » mais explore une tragédie émotionnelle complexe, rendant Hulk incontrôlable et destructeur après des années de maîtrise forcée.
- L’angle du traumatisme psychologique plutôt que du fan-service relance potentiellement un arc dramatique pour Hulk, questionnant son avenir dans l’univers Marvel.

articles.title: Suspected Chinese-Speaking Hackers Target Central Asian Governments With OctLurk and SilkLurk
articles.text:
A Chinese-speaking threat actor is suspected to be behind a fresh wave of cyber attacks targeting government organizations mainly located in Central Asia, including Afghanistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and the Syrian Arab Republic, since January 2025.
These targeted organizations operate across several sectors, such as healthcare, research, government offices, ministries of foreign affairs, logistics, law-enforcement agencies, urban planning and facilities management, and public educational establishments, per Kaspersky. The activity has not been linked to any known adversary or group.
The attacks are characterized by the use of two new obfuscated backdoors the Russian cybersecurity company is tracking as OctLurk and SilkLurk, as well as a specialized utility codenamed LurkProxy to proxy network traffic.
"OctLurk and SilkLurk can download and inject additional plugins to perform further malicious actions, including launching command shells, performing file system activity, synthesizing keyboard and mouse events, network scanning, credential dumping, keylogging, password theft from browsers, email collection, and remote access," researchers Saurabh Sharma and Yaroslav Kikel said.
The initial access vector used in these attacks is currently unknown. However, Kaspersky's analysis has found that OctLurk is injected into memory and deployed by means of a loader, with the attackers also checking internet connectivity to the domain "dns.ssentialserv[.]xyz" before executing a batch script responsible for launching LurkProxy. The tool then establishes contact with a remote server ("154.196.162[.]76") for command-and-control (C2).
Once run, OctoLurk first collects system information, encrypts it, and sends it to a hard-coded C2 server ("dns.multitoconference[.]com") over a stream socket connection. It's equipped to load plugins received from the server directly into memory to enable command execution, file operations, clipboard content gathering and modification, screenshot capture, and mouse movements.
The threat actors have been found to leverage the backdoor's command shell plugin to perform the following series of actions -
- Fingerprint the host and harvest extensive data about the compromised system.
- Run commands to export successful logon events for remote interactive logons and to query those events for specific users.
- Harvest password hashes from domain controllers using Impacket's "secretsdump.py" tool.
- Drop and execute a keylogger that masquerades as AnyDesk to sidestep detection.
- Decrypt and extract passwords from Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox.
- Establish remote access to the victim machine using Pandora RC agent.
- Scan internal and public networks using Fscan to identify services running on specific ports, such as Secure Shell (SSH) on port 22 and MySQL on port 3306, and then attempt to access these services using credentials from a password file named "pp.txt."
- Connect to an email server, authenticate with a username and password, and issue commands to collect or manipulate emails.
LurkProxy, for its part, can function as a reverse proxy in two distinct modes, either as a SOCKS5 proxy or a transparent proxy. At any given time, the malware can operate in only one mode to route network traffic through a target address.
The third tool in the threat actor's arsenal is SilkLurk, which is launched by means of a DLL that, in turn, is executed using a DLL side-loading sequence. The backdoor then creates a TCP socket and connects to a C2 server specified in its configuration, followed by collecting victim information and transmitting it to the server.
In response, the server sends a command that's to be executed on the infected endpoint. This can involve getting the system's local time, setting a sleep interval that determines the frequency at which the backdoor polls the C2 server, sending or updating backdoor configuration, and receiving and injecting additional plugins into memory.
The post-compromise activity linked to SilkLurk is below -
- Invoke "cmd.exe" to launch PowerShell and run commands to connect to shared network resources with administrative credentials, search and stage confidential documents, disconnect from the network shares, and use legitimate archiving tools like WinRAR and 7-Zip to archive the stolen data.
- Run "cmd.exe" to initiate a DLL side-loading chain to drop PlugX, a known backdoor used by Chinese hacking groups.
Kaspersky said it found infrastructure overlaps between the campaign and a prior set of attacks involving a C++-based implant codenamed SilentRaid (aka MystRodX and TrustFall).
"This overlap points to shared infrastructure across multiple OS-targeting campaigns, though it remains unclear whether these activities ran concurrently or at different times," Kaspersky said. "The emergence of the OctLurk and SilkLurk multi-plugin malware framework highlights how threat actors continuously refine their tactics to evade detection and maintain control over compromised networks."
"Both families operate primarily in memory, leaving only a minimalistic loader on disk that relies on machine-specific data (OctLurk uses the drive serial number, and SilkLurk uses the computer name) to decode payload locations and contents. This victim-specific encoding makes reverse engineering and automated detection considerably harder."

articles.title: Éclipse solaire totale, Perséides, éclipse de Lune : tout ce qu'il faut observer dans le ciel en août 2026 (CALENDRIER COMPLET)
articles.text:
Ça y est, nous sommes en août 2026, et je l’avoue, c’est le mois que j’ai attendu avec le plus d’impatience depuis le début de l’année. Les astronomes et les passionnés se sont préparés depuis longtemps aux phénomènes qui sont prévus ces prochaines semaines, à commencer par une éclipse solaire totale remarquable qui va se produire en Europe. Pour laquelle il est absolument indispensable de s’équiper en lunettes d’éclipse : vous en trouverez dans notre guide dédié (et vraiment, j’insiste, ne tardez pas à vous en procurer).
Mais cette éclipse solaire n’est pas le seul phénomène qui va rendre ce mois d’août 2026 inoubliable. Alors, espérons que la météo soit au beau fixe, parce qu’il va y avoir de quoi se régaler, en pleines vacances d’été pour beaucoup de monde. Voici le programme complet !
Les dates des phases de la Lune en août 2026
On commence avec la base : les phases de la Lune, tout au long du mois d’août — le cycle lunaire est toujours un beau spectacle à admirer !
- Le jeudi 6 août, c’est la phase du dernier quartier de Lune.
- Le mercredi 12 août correspond à la nouvelle Lune. Et, cette fois-ci, il y a aussi une éclipse solaire (restez, je vous en parle plus en détails dans la suite de cet article) !
- Le jeudi 20 août, c’est le premier quartier de Lune.
- Pour voir la pleine Lune, ce mois-ci ce sera le vendredi 28 août.
Toutes les planètes visibles à l’œil nu
Plusieurs planètes du système solaire sont visibles à l’œil nu en août 2026.
- Depuis mars, et jusqu’en août, Vénus est visible le soir vers l’ouest. Profitez de ces dernières semaines pour observer l’Étoile du Berger, on ne la retrouvera qu’en novembre 2026.
- Profitez aussi de Saturne, qui entame une période de visibilité toute la nuit, d’août à décembre 2026. On s’approche de son opposition, le 4 octobre.
- La petite Mercure est visible par intermittence : on peut la voir jusqu’au 15 août, le matin.
- Mars est également visible ce mois-ci.
- Jupiter sera de retour en octobre 2026 ; encore un peu de patience !
Les autres phénomènes astronomiques d’août 2026 en France
C’est assurément LE mois de l’année 2026 pour tourner les yeux vers le ciel. Croisez les doigts avec moi pour que la météo soit clémente, car il va y avoir beaucoup de phénomènes astronomiques magnifiques à observer.
- Depuis le vendredi 31 juillet et jusqu’au mardi 4 août, le Soleil se couche dans l’Arc de Triomphe à Paris. Un événement qui attire souvent des photographes qui espèrent immortaliser ce coucher de Soleil unique dans l’Arc de Triomphe. C’est aussi très beau à simplement observer. Mais attention à l’éblouissement, attendez que le Soleil soit assez bas pour le regarder ; gare aussi aux voitures, dans cette zone très fréquentée de Paris !
- Du vendredi 7 au dimanche 9 août, ce sont les Nuits des étoiles en France. La période est idéale pour observer la voûte céleste en compagnie de scientifiques et d’associations. Tous les événements organisés en France sont recensés sur cette carte.
- Si vous ne devez regarder qu’un phénomène astronomique, c’est celui-ci : le soir du mercredi 12 août 2026, une éclipse solaire est visible en France. C’est LE plus beau rendez-vous astronomique de l’été. Tout l’hexagone peut admirer le phénomène dans sa phase partielle : vous pouvez consulter cette carte montrant le pourcentage d’occultation du Soleil selon les villes françaises. Et, bien sûr, n’oubliez pas vos lunettes d’éclipse pour ne prendre aucun risque pour vos yeux !
- Dans la nuit du mercredi 12 au jeudi 13 août, c’est le pic d’activité des Perséides. L’opportunité est trop belle cette année : ce maximum d’activité survient quelques heures après l’éclipse solaire, et donc lors d’une nuit sans Lune. Les conditions d’observation sont idéales.
- Le vendredi 28 août, une éclipse partielle de Lune se produit. La France métropolitaine est dans la zone de visibilité du phénomène. Deux éclipses à un intervalle si court, ce n’est pas si étonnant, et cela s’est même déjà produit l’an dernier : les Français avaient pu voir 2 éclipses en mars 2025.
L’éclipse solaire totale du 12 août 2026 : l’événement astronomique de la décennie
Observer une éclipse solaire est un événement rare, que l’on n’oublie pas. Surtout quand c’est une éclipse totale. La probabilité est d’en voir une est faible : une occultation totale du Soleil par la Lune ne survient que tous les 400 ans au même endroit sur la Terre.
La prochaine éclipse solaire est donc une véritable aubaine. Elle a lieu le mercredi 12 août 2026, et l’Europe est aux premières loges pour l’admirer. En Espagne ou en Islande, le phénomène s’annonce splendide : la bande de totalité de l’éclipse passe sur ces pays. Cela vaut donc le coup de songer à organiser vos vacances sur la trajectoire de l’éclipse.
En France métropolitaine, l’éclipse du 12 août sera toujours partielle, mais pas moins belle. Le Soleil sera occulté jusqu’à 99 % en fonction des lieux d’observation.
Lunettes d’éclipse solaire : le guide complet de Numerama pour ne pas se tromper
Pour profiter d’un tel phénomène astronomique, il est indispensable de s’équiper. Il ne faut JAMAIS regarder le Soleil sans protection adaptée. Des lunettes d’éclipse aux normes sont requises pour observer le Soleil disparaître derrière la Lune.
Attention à ne pas vous tromper lors de l’achat, car des lunettes d’éclipse non conformes sont disponibles à la vente en France, comme l’a constaté l’Association Française d’Astronomie (AFA) : utiliser de tels équipements représente un risque réel pour vos yeux.
Il est indispensable de vérifier la certification de vos lunettes avant usage. Vous pouvez aussi vous référer à notre guide d’achat sur Numerama : tous les modèles suggérés sont aux normes. ⬇️

articles.title: Se filtra el Pixel Tag: la alternativa de Google al AirTag y Moto Tag llegará muy pronto
articles.text: Le ha llevado mucho más tiempo de lo que la mayoría pensaba, pero Google está lista para lanzar el Pixel Tag , su alternativa a productos como los AirTag, Moto Tag y Xiaomi Tag. Así lo indica una nueva filtración que incluso ha entregado una primera imagen del producto, cuyo lanzamiento sería inminente. Según reporta 9to5Google , ya se habían encontrado referencias al Pixel Tag en leaks de los Pixel 11. Sin embargo, hasta aquí no se sabía nada respecto del producto o de sus características. Pero eso ha cambiado a falta de pocos días para la presentación formal de la nueva línea de hardware de Google. El Pixel Tag ha comenzado a aparecer listado en tiendas alemanas, aunque prácticamente sin detalles. Pero el citado medio dio con una web eslovena que publicó una descripción del producto, pintando una imagen bastante clara respecto de cuál es su finalidad, más allá de no revelar detalles técnicos específicos. En la imagen que se ha publicado se observa un Pixel Tab de color gris plateado con el isotipo de Google. El dispositivo tiene un formato oblongo similar al del Xiaomi Tag , aunque algo más angosto y sin una anilla para colgar. Esto hace pensar que puede llegar acompañado de accesorios para usarlo como llavero o llevarlo colgado en una cartera, maleta o mochila, como sucede con el AirTag de Apple. Google está por lanzar el Pixel Tag, su propio rastreador Si bien no se han revelado detalles específicos del apartado técnico del Pixel Tag, es lógico creer que ofrecerá prestaciones similares a las de otros productos ya disponibles en el mercado. Uno de los grandes puntos a favor de Google para lanzar su propio rastreador es que puede aprovechar la integración con la plataforma Localizador (Find Hub), que permite encontrar dispositivos como móviles, tablets, relojes inteligentes o auriculares a través de una conexión Bluetooth. En la descripción eslovena sí se indica que el Google Pixel Tag dispone de un altavoz para hacerlo sonar cuando está cerca y encontrarlo más fácil. Más allá de eso, todavía no se sabe si está equipado con soporte para banda ultraancha (UWB), o si utiliza una pila reemplazable. Vale mencionar que en una de las tiendas alemanas donde aparece listado se usa el nombre Google Tag, en lugar de Pixel Tag. En tanto que en otra tienda indica un precio de 25,60 euros , aunque no se sabe si es certero. Suponiendo que el dato esté correcto, lo ubicaría debajo del Moto Tag 2 (39,99 euros) y el AirTag de Apple (35 euros). Y si bien sería más caro que el Xiaomi Tag , que se consigue en Europa por unos 15 euros, no estaría nada mal para ser un producto oficial de Google. Si los de Mountain View realmente lanzan el Pixel Tag, el timing de las filtraciones apunta a que podría ser el próximo 12 de agosto , durante la presentación de los Pixel 11. Seguir leyendo: Se filtra el Pixel Tag: la alternativa de Google al AirTag y Moto Tag llegará muy pronto

articles.title: Google retire en urgence l'IA de Google Earth après la création de fausses images satellites
articles.text:
Zoomer sur un lieu, taper une phrase, et voir une scène se dessiner par-dessus la vraie image satellite : un immeuble disparu, un quartier futur, une catastrophe. Sur le papier, la fonction visait surtout les enseignants et les professionnels du géospatial. Google a activé cet outil le 30 juillet 2026 dans la version web de Google Earth, avant de le retirer dès le lendemain.
    Pour aller plus loin
            Voici à quoi ressemblerait Paris avec des climatiseurs et des dragons : Google intègre Nano Banana à Google Earth
            
Concrètement, il s’agissait d’un bouton « créer une image » ajouté à Earth sur le web. L’idée était de choisir un endroit, de décrire ce qu’on souhaitait y voir, et le modèle Nano Banana 2 renvoyait une image photoréaliste construite à partir des vues satellite, aériennes et 3D de Google.
L’IA s’appuyait sur les vraies données géographiques du lieu. C’est justement ce qui rendait le résultat crédible, et donc dangereux.
Un faux site nucléaire en une phrase
Henk van Ess, spécialiste de l’investigation en source ouverte, a publié sa démonstration quelques heures après le lancement. Sa liste : des réfugiés à la frontière mexicaine, une centrale nucléaire en Iran, un accident mortel dans une rue d’Amsterdam, un cratère de bombe à côté d’un hôpital à Gaza. De son côté, NPR a fabriqué des images d’inondations autour du Capitole et d’incendies sur un terminal pétrolier iranien. Comme l’a détaillé The Verge, ces scènes n’avaient jamais eu lieu, mais s’affichaient sur des coordonnées bien réelles.
Face aux critiques, Google a d’abord défendu sa fonction. Dans un message sur X, l’entreprise a rappelé que chaque image portait un filigrane SynthID : une marque invisible, insérée dans les pixels, qui signale un contenu généré par IA et reste vérifiable via l’application Gemini ou Lens. En pratique, l’argument tient mal. La plupart des gens ne prennent pas le temps de vérifier une image avant de la partager, et, dans plusieurs tests, Gemini lui-même n’a pas su reconnaître une image générée par l’IA de Google.
Google parle désormais de renforcer les garde-fous avant un éventuel retour, et précise que ces images n’apparaîtraient pas dans l’expérience Earth des autres utilisateurs : elles circulaient surtout via des captures d’écran.

articles.title: Fridays With Bob
articles.text:
When I started at Spectrum 25 years ago, a senior editor suggested that I find a “rabbi,” by which he meant someone who could mentor me in how EEs approach problems and evaluate potential solutions.
I didn’t find one right away. Then in 2005 we decided to do a special report, focusing on the challenges of enterprise software development. I suggested we invite IEEE Life Senior Member Robert N. Charette, a self-described risk ecologist, prolific book author, and leading authority on risk management and software engineering, to explore in our pages the myriad reasons software projects fail. His seminal article “Why Software Fails” is still read in university engineering classes today.
IEEE Life Senior Member Robert N. Charette is one of IEEE Spectrum’s most prolific authors.Robert N. Charette
It was, as they say, the beginning of a beautiful friendship. I had found my rabbi, one who shared my love of writing. We settled into a rhythm that would last more than 20 years, talking on Friday mornings about a range of topics including the growing ubiquity of software in our lives.
So when I became Spectrum’s website editor in 2007, he was the first contributor I tapped to start a regular blog (remember those?). The Risk Factor was born and over the course of more than 10 years and 1,750 posts, Bob chronicled hundreds of software debacles, culminating in “Lessons From a Decade of IT Failures,” which won a Jesse H. Neal Award for Best Infographics in 2016. Ironically, yet predictably, those infographics were created in a software package that is no longer supported and thus are lost to the bits of time.
“I like the expression on the fish just before it’s going to be swallowed by the heron.”Robert N. Charette
Bob, however, was not a one-trick pony. In between his full-time job running his two management consultancies and raising a future biochemist and a future civil engineer, his daughters Maura and Megan, he also wrote many deeply reported and insightful articles. These include last year’s “The Doctor Will See Your Electronic Health Record Now,” the eye-opening 12-part series and e-book The EV Transition Explained, and my personal favorite “Automated to Death,” about the deadly consequences of the automation paradox as manifested by the cyberphysical systems that pilot planes, trains, and automobiles.
“The young bald eagle I photographed in September 2024 had bands that I could read which identified it as a female born in May 2024, near Lexington Park, St. Mary’s County, Maryland, about 65 miles away from where I live.”Robert N. Charette
His main goal all along has been to make software visible, as he told me one Friday in July. “Software is all around us, but we don’t recognize it at all,” he said. “I really wanted my stories to help people better understand complex software systems. You can’t see software, you can’t touch it, you can’t taste it. You may feel the consequences of software failure, but you never see the reason itself.”
When he told me that he was hanging up his hat as a contributing editor to focus on nature photography and to write a handful of fictional trilogies, including one entitled “The STEM Murders” featuring an engineer-turned-detective and his rabbi, I asked him which of his Spectrum articles had the biggest impact.
“The hummingbird I caught with the yellow of a road curb behind it.”Robert N. Charette
He singled out the 2013 feature “The STEM Crisis Is a Myth.” “Spectrum gave me a platform to question the assumption that we needed more STEM graduates. Until then, people didn’t really realize how much of the STEM crisis was a mythology that was perpetuated by employers and the academic community and was foisted on the IEEE community,” he said.
Charette made a career of questioning assumptions. The best way to mitigate risk, he told me as our Friday chat drew to a close, is to be careful making assumptions in the first place. “My main risk maxim is assumptions made are risks accepted.”
